employment.en: The work or occupation for which one is used, and often paid
employment.ee: The personnel director handled the whole employment procedure

entrepreneur.en: A person who organizes and operates a business venture and assumes much of the associated risk.

expenditure.en: Act of expending or paying out.
expenditure.ee: The expenditure of time, money, and political capital on this project has been excessive.

export.ee: Oil is the main export of Saudi Arabia.

import.en: Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade.
import.ee: It was a matter of great import.

income.en: Money one earns by working or by capitalising on the work of others.

inflation.en: An act, instance of, or state of expansion or increase in size, especially by injection of a gas.
inflation.ee: The inflation of the balloon took five hours.

investment.en: The act of investing, or state of being invested.
investment.ee: Giving your children a good education is a wise long-term investment.

liability.en: An obligation, debt or responsibility owed to someone.

monopoly.en: A situation, by legal privilege or other agreement, in which solely one party (company, cartel etc.) exclusively provides a particular product or service, dominating that market and generally exerting powerful control over it.
monopoly.ee: A land monopoly renders its holder(s) nearly almighty in an agricultural society.

outsourcing.en: To transfer the management and/or day-to-day execution of a business function to a third-party service provider.
outsourcing.ee: They decided to outsource the design and manufacture of the system to a vendor.

productivity.en: The state of being productive, fertile or efficient
productivity.ee: You can see the computer age everywhere but in the productivity statistics.

profit.en: Total income or cash flow minus expenditures. The money or other benefit a non-governmental organization or individual receives in exchange for products and services sold at an advertised price.
profit.ee: Reading such an enlightening book on the subject was of much profit to his studies.

property.ee: Important types of property include real property (land), personal property (other physical possessions), and intellectual property (rights over artistic creations, inventions, etc.).

recession.en: The act or an instance of receding or withdrawing.

regulation.en: The act of regulating or the condition of being regulated.

revenue.en: The income returned by an investment.

subsidy.en: Financial support or assistance, such as a grant.
subsidy.ee: Manufacturing firms are supported by government subsidies in some countries.

surplus.en: That which remains when use or need is satisfied, or when a limit is reached; excess; overplus.
surplus.ee: It is surplus to our needs

tariff.en: A system of government-imposed duties levied on imported or exported goods; a list of such duties, or the duties themselves.

tax.en: Money paid to the government other than for transaction-specific goods and services.
tax.ee: a heavy tax on time or health

wage.en: (often in plural) An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
wage.ee: Before her promotion, her wages were 20% less.

accounting.ee: He was required to give a thorough accounting of his time.

acquisition.en: The act or process of acquiring.
acquisition.ee: The acquisition of sports equipment can be fun in itself.

arbitrage.en: A market activity in which a security, commodity, currency or other tradable item is bought in one market and sold simultaneously in another, in order to profit from price differences between the markets.

competition.ee: The competition for this job is strong.

crowdfunding.en: Funding by many individuals pooling their money together for a common goal, usually via the Internet.

depreciation.en: The state of being depreciated; disparagement.

equity.en: Fairness, impartiality, or justice as determined in light of "natural law" or "natural right".

insurance.en: A means of indemnity against a future occurrence of an uncertain event.
insurance.ee: The car was totalled, but fortunately I had insurance.

leverage.en: A force compounded by means of a lever rotating around a pivot; see torque.
leverage.ee: A crowbar uses leverage to pry nails out of wood.

pension.en: An annuity paid regularly as benefit due to a retired employee, serviceman etc. in consideration of past services, originally and chiefly by a government but also by various private pension schemes.
pension.ee: Many old people depend on their pension to pay the bills.

portfolio.en: A case for carrying papers, drawings, photographs, maps and other flat documents.
portfolio.ee: I would like to introduce you to our portfolio of services.

remittance.en: The act of transmitting money, bills, etc. to a distant place, in return or payment for goods purchased.

stagflation.en: Inflation accompanied by stagnant growth, unemployment or recession.

aging.en: To cause to grow old; to impart the characteristics of age to.

allergy.en: A disorder of the immune system causing adverse reactions to substances (allergens) not harmful to most and marked by the body's production of histamines and associated with atopy, anaphylaxis, and asthma.

antibiotic.en: Any substance that can destroy or inhibit the growth of bacteria and similar microorganisms, generally transported by the lymphatic system.

anxiety.en: An unpleasant state of mental uneasiness, nervousness, apprehension and obsession or concern about some uncertain event.

autism.en: A pervasive neurological disorder that is observable in early childhood and persists throughout the lifespan, characterised by atypical communication, language development, eye contact, and sensory experiences.

bacteria.en: A type, species, or strain of bacterium.

burnout.en: The experience of long-term exhaustion and diminished interest, especially in one's career.

cancer.en: A disease in which the cells of a tissue undergo uncontrolled (and often rapid) proliferation.

cardiovascular.en: Relating to the circulatory system, that is the heart and blood vessels.

contraception.en: The use of a device or procedure to prevent conception as a result of sexual activity.

depression.en: In psychotherapy and psychiatry, a state of mind producing serious, long-term lowering of enjoyment of life or inability to visualize a happy future.
depression.ee: I used to suffer from depression, but now I'm mostly content with my life.

diabetes.en: Diabetes insipidus; any condition characterized by excessive or incontinent urine, now specifically as caused by impaired production of, or response to, the antidiuretic hormone vasopressin.

diagnosis.en: To determine which disease is causing a sick person's signs and symptoms; to find the diagnosis.
diagnosis.ee: He was given the wrong treatment due to an erroneous diagnosis.

diet.en: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
diet.ee: The diet of the Giant Panda consists mainly of bamboo.

disability.en: State of being disabled; deprivation or want of ability; absence of competent physical, intellectual, or moral power, means, fitness, and the like.

disease.en: An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired.
disease.ee: The tomato plants had some kind of disease that left their leaves splotchy and fruit withered.

epidemic.en: A widespread disease that affects many individuals in a population.
epidemic.ee: Epidemic hysteria occurred upon the incumbent’s reelection.

exercise.en: Any activity designed to develop or hone a skill or ability.
exercise.ee: The teacher told us that the next exercise is to write an essay.

fertility.en: The condition, or the degree, of being fertile.
fertility.ee: Muckspreading increases the fertility of the soil.

genetics.en: The branch of biology that deals with the transmission and variation of inherited characteristics, in particular chromosomes and DNA.

healthcare.en: The prevention, treatment, and management of illness or the preservation of mental and physical well-being through the services offered by the medical, nursing, and allied health professions.
healthcare.ee: I think free health care should also cover nearsightedness.

hormone.en: Any substance produced by one tissue and conveyed by the bloodstream to another to effect physiological activity.

hospital.en: A large medical facility, usually in a building with multiple floors, where seriously ill or injured patients are given extensive medical and/or surgical treatment.

hygiene.en: The science of health, its promotion and preservation.
hygiene.ee: Hygiene is an important consideration in places where food is prepared.

immunization.en: The process by which an individual is safely exposed in a controlled manner to a material that is designed to prime their immune system against that material.
immunization.ee: Immunization against influenza is important for all child-care workers.

infection.en: The act or process of infecting.

inflammation.en: The act of inflaming, kindling, or setting on fire.
inflammation.ee: an inflammation of the mind, of the body politic, or of parties

insomnia.en: A sleeping disorder that is known for its symptoms of unrest and the inability to sleep.

lifestyle.en: A style of living that reflects the attitudes and values of a person or group.

medication.en: A medicine, or all the medicines regularly taken by a patient.

metabolism.en: The chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.

mortality.en: The state or quality of being mortal.

nutrition.en: The organic process by which an organism assimilates food and uses it for growth and maintenance.

obesity.en: The state of being obese due to an excess of body fat.

organ.en: A larger part of an organism, composed of tissues that perform similar functions.

outbreak.en: An eruption; the sudden appearance of a rash, disease, etc.
outbreak.ee: Any epidemic outbreak causes understandable panic.

patient.en: A person or animal who receives treatment from a doctor or other medically educated person.
patient.ee: The subject of a passive verb is usually a patient.

placebo.en: A dummy medicine containing no active ingredients; an inert treatment.

prevention.en: The act of preventing or hindering; obstruction of action, access, or approach; thwarting.

quarantine.en: The desert in which Christ fasted for 40 days according to the Bible.

rehabilitation.en: The process of rehabilitating somebody or something.

sanitation.en: The hygienic disposal or recycling of waste.

stress.ee: Go easy on him, he's been under a lot of stress lately.

surgery.en: A procedure involving major incisions to remove, repair, or replace a part of a body.
surgery.ee: Many times surgery is necessary to prevent cancer from spreading.

symptoms.en: A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash.

therapy.en: Attempted remediation of a health problem following a diagnosis, usually synonymous with treatment.

vaccine.en: A substance given to stimulate the body's production of antibodies and provide immunity against a disease without causing the disease itself in the treatment, prepared from the agent that causes the disease (or a related, also effective, but safer disease), or a synthetic substitute.

virus.en: A submicroscopic, non-cellular structure consisting of a core of DNA or RNA surrounded by a protein coat, that requires a living host cell to replicate, and often causes disease in the host organism.
virus.ee: He caught a virus and had to stay home from school.

acupuncture.en: The insertion of needles into the (living) tissue of the body, especially for purposes of pain relief.

antibody.en: A protein produced by B-lymphocytes that binds to a specific antigen.

antidepressant.en: An agent that prevents or counteracts depression.

arthritis.en: Inflammation of a joint or joints causing pain and/or disability, swelling and stiffness, and due to various causes such as infection, trauma, degenerative changes or metabolic disorders.

asthma.en: A long-term respiratory condition, in which the airways may unexpectedly and suddenly narrow, often in response to an allergen, cold air, exercise, or emotional stress. Symptoms include wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing.

cholesterol.en: A sterol lipid synthesized by the liver and transported in the bloodstream to the membranes of all animal cells; it plays a central role in many biochemical processes and, as a lipoprotein that coats the walls of blood vessels, is associated with cardiovascular disease.
cholesterol.ee: improve your cholesterol; lower your cholesterol

coma.en: A state of unconsciousness from which one may not wake up, usually induced by some form of trauma.

complication.en: The act or process of complicating.

congenital.en: (of a trait or a disease) Present since birth.

dehydration.en: The act or process of removing water from something.

dementia.en: A progressive decline in cognitive function due to damage or disease in the brain beyond what might be expected from normal aging. Areas particularly affected include memory, attention, judgement, language and problem solving.

dna.en: The part of a living being that carries genetic information.

dosage.en: The administration of a medication etc, in a measured amount; dosing.

endocrine.en: The secretion of an endocrine gland.

fatigue.en: A weariness caused by exertion; exhaustion.

fracture.en: An instance of breaking, a place where something has broken.

germ.en: The small mass of cells from which a new organism develops; a seed, bud or spore.

hallucination.en: A sensory perception of something that does not exist, often arising from disorder of the nervous system, as in delirium tremens; a delusion.

hypertension.en: The disease or disorder of abnormally high blood pressure.

immunity.en: The state of being insusceptible to something; notably:
immunity.ee: Superbugs are bacteria that develop an immunity to antibiotics.

insulin.en: A polypeptide hormone that regulates carbohydrate metabolism.

malpractice.en: The improper treatment of a patient by a physician that results in injury or loss.

nurse.ee: They hired a nurse to care for their young boy.

oncology.en: The branch of medicine concerned with tumors, including study of their development, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

parasite.en: A person who lives on other people's efforts or expense and gives little or nothing back.
parasite.ee: Lice, fleas, ticks and mites are widely spread parasites.

pathogen.en: Any organism or substance, especially a microorganism, capable of causing disease, such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa or fungi. Microorganisms are not considered to be pathogenic until they have reached a population size that is large enough to cause disease.

pneumonia.en: An acute or chronic inflammation of the lungs caused by viruses, bacteria or other microorganisms, or sometimes by physical or chemical irritants.

prescription.en: The act of prescribing a rule, law, etc..
prescription.ee: "Jurisdiction to prescribe" is a state's authority to make its laws applicable to certain persons or activities. -- Richard G. Alexander, Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996: Congress exceeds its jurisdiction to prescribe law. Washington and Lee Law Review, 1997.

prognosis.en: A forecast of the future course of a disease or disorder, based on medical knowledge.

protein.en: Any of numerous large, complex naturally-produced molecules composed of one or more long chains of amino acids, in which the amino acid groups are held together by peptide bonds.

recovery.en: The act or process of regaining or repossession of something lost.

screening.en: To filter by passing through a screen.
screening.ee: Mary screened the beans to remove the clumps of gravel.

specialist.en: Someone who is an expert in, or devoted to, some specific branch of study or research.
specialist.ee: The tree Lepidothamnus laxifolius is a high alpine specialist found in high-altitude bog communities and in scrub.

treatment.en: The process or manner of treating someone or something.
treatment.ee: He still has nightmares resulting from the treatment he received from his captors.

tuberculosis.en: An infectious disease of humans and animals caused by a species of mycobacterium, usually Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mainly infecting the lungs where it causes tubercles characterized by the expectoration of mucus and sputum, fever, weight loss, and chest pain, and transmitted through inhalation or ingestion of bacteria.

tumor.en: An abnormal growth; differential diagnosis includes abscess, metaplasia, and neoplasia.

assessment.en: The act of assessing or an amount (of tax, levy or duty etc) assessed.

classroom.en: A room, often in a school, where classes take place

curriculum.en: The set of courses, coursework, and their content, offered at a school or university.

degree.en: A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university or, in some countries, a college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.)
degree.ee: She has two bachelor's degrees and is studying towards a master's degree.

enrollment.en: The act of enrolling or the state of being enrolled.

extracurricular.en: An activity outside the normal academic curriculum.
extracurricular.ee: The students enjoy a number of extracurricular activities at weekends.

faculty.en: The academic staff at schools, colleges, universities or not-for-profit research institutes, as opposed to the students or support staff.
faculty.ee: She transferred from the Faculty of Science to the Faculty of Medicine.

graduate.en: A person who is recognized by a university as having completed the requirements of a degree studied at the institution.
graduate.ee: If the government wants graduates to stay in the country they should offer more incentives.

homework.en: Work that is done at home, especially school exercises assigned by a teacher.
homework.ee: You must do your homework before you can watch television.

instruction.en: The act of instructing, teaching, or furnishing with information or knowledge.
instruction.ee: Instruction will be provided on how to handle difficult customers.

lecture.en: A spoken lesson or exposition, usually delivered to a group.
lecture.ee: During class today the professor delivered an interesting lecture.

postgraduate.en: A person continuing to study in a field after having successfully completed a degree course.

semester.en: Half of a school year or academic year such as fall or spring semester.

syllabus.en: A summary of topics which will be covered during an academic course, or a text or lecture.

tuition.en: A sum of money paid for instruction (such as in a high school, boarding school, university, or college).
tuition.ee: These rosemaling workshops are no place for anyone who wants to pester me or the students with the "white privilege" card, inter alia. Therefore, I reserve the right to refund the tuition of such men and women, kick them out the door, and bar them from at least two of my future events.

tutoring.en: To instruct or teach, especially an individual or small group.
tutoring.ee: To help pay her tuition, the college student began to tutor high school students in calculus and physics.

university.en: Institution of higher education (typically accepting students from the age of about 17 or 18, depending on country, but in some exceptional cases able to take younger students) where subjects are studied and researched in depth and degrees are offered.
university.ee: The only reason why I haven't gone to university is because I can't afford it.

workshop.en: A room, especially one which is not particularly large, used for manufacturing or other light industrial work.

campus.en: The grounds or property of a school, college, university, business, church, or hospital, often understood to include buildings and other structures.
campus.ee: The campus is sixty hectares in size.

concentration.en: The act, process or ability of concentrating; the process of becoming concentrated, or the state of being concentrated.

debate.en: An argument, or discussion, usually in an ordered or formal setting, often with more than two people, generally ending with a vote or other decision.
debate.ee: After a four-hour debate, the committee voted to table the motion.

elective.en: Something that is an option or that may be elected, like a course of tertiary study or a medical procedure.
elective.ee: My insurance wouldn't pay for the operation because it was elective surgery.

engagement.en: An appointment, especially to speak or perform.
engagement.ee: The lecturer has three speaking engagements this week.

evaluation.en: An assessment, such as an annual personnel performance review used as the basis for a salary increase or bonus, or a summary of a particular situation.

grade.ee: I gave him a good grade for effort.

grant.en: The act of granting; a bestowing or conferring; concession; allowance; permission.
grant.ee: I got a grant from the government to study archeology in Egypt.

internship.en: A job taken by a student in order to learn a profession or trade.

laboratory.en: A room, building or institution equipped for scientific research, experimentation or analysis.

library.en: An institution which holds books and/or other forms of media for use by the public or qualified people often lending them out, as well as providing various other services for its users.

memorization.en: The act of committing something to memory or memorizing.

numeracy.en: The quality of being numerate; numerical skill.

quota.en: A proportional part or share; the share or proportion assigned to each in a division.

recall.en: The action or fact of calling someone or something back.
recall.ee: He was recalled to service after his retirement.

reform.en: The change of something that is defective, broken, inefficient or otherwise negative, in order to correct or improve it
reform.ee: A major reform is needed to improve the efficiency in the factory.

self-assessment.en: Assessment of oneself (especially of ones income tax)

simulation.en: Something that simulates a system or environment in order to predict actual behaviour.
simulation.ee: The most reliable simulation predicts that the hurricane will turn north.

stipend.en: A scholarship granted to a student.
stipend.ee: My stipend for doing public service is barely enough to cover living expenses.

undergraduate.en: A student at a university who has not yet received a degree.
undergraduate.ee: After completing my undergraduate studies, I embarked on a career in publishing.

adaptation.en: The process of adapting something or becoming adapted to a situation; adjustment, modification.

asteroid.en: Any member of the taxonomic class Asteroidea; a starfish

astronomy.en: The study of the physical universe beyond the Earth's atmosphere, including the process of mapping locations and properties of the matter and radiation in the universe.

atom.en: The smallest possible amount of matter which still retains its identity as a chemical element, now known to consist of a nucleus surrounded by electrons.
atom.ee: In a Venn diagram, an atom is depicted as an area circumscribed by lines but not cut by any line.

biochemistry.en: The chemistry of those compounds that occur in living organisms, and the processes that occur in their metabolism and catabolism
biochemistry.ee: The biochemistries of fungal and bacterial cells are quite distinct.

biology.en: The study of all life or living matter.

botany.en: The scientific study of plants, a branch of biology. Typically those disciplines that involve the whole plant.

catalyst.en: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process.
catalyst.ee: Economic development and integration are working as a catalyst for peace.

cell.en: A single-room dwelling for a hermit.
cell.ee: Gregor Mendel must have spent a good amount of time outside of his cell.

chemistry.en: The branch of natural science that deals with the composition and constitution of substances and the changes that they undergo as a consequence of alterations in the constitution of their molecules.

chromosome.en: A linear arrangement of condensed DNA and associated proteins (such as chaperone proteins) which contains the genetic material (genome) of an organism.

circulation.en: The act of moving in a circle, or in a course which brings the moving body to the place where its motion began.
circulation.ee: The new bills will come into circulation next Friday.

cloning.ee: The scientists were able to clone a sheep.

combustion.en: The act or process of burning.

compound.en: An enclosure within which workers, prisoners, or soldiers are confined

conductivity.en: The ability of a material to conduct electricity, heat, fluid or sound

crystal.en: A solid composed of an array of atoms or molecules possessing long-range order and arranged in a pattern which is periodic in three dimensions.

deduction.en: That which is deducted; that which is subtracted or removed
deduction.ee: You might want to donate the old junk and just take the deduction.

density.en: A measure of the mass of matter contained by a unit volume.
density.ee: The number of particles per unit volume of a specified volume can be considered to be the particle density for the specified volume.

diffusion.en: The act of diffusing or dispersing something, or the property of being diffused or dispersed; dispersion.

ecology.en: The branch of biology dealing with the relationships of organisms with their environment and with each other.

electricity.en: Originally, a property of amber and certain other nonconducting substances to attract lightweight material when rubbed, or the cause of this property; now understood to be a phenomenon caused by the distribution and movement of charged subatomic particles and their interaction with the electromagnetic field.
electricity.ee: Opening night for the new production had an electricity unlike other openings.

electrolysis.en: The chemical change produced by passing an electric current through a conducting solution or a molten salt.

electron.en: The subatomic particle having a negative charge and orbiting the nucleus; the flow of electrons in a conductor constitutes electricity.

element.en: One of the simplest or essential parts or principles of which anything consists, or upon which the constitution or fundamental powers of anything are based.
element.ee: Letters are the elements of written language.

energy.en: The impetus behind all motion and all activity.

enzyme.en: A globular protein that catalyses a biological chemical reaction.

evaporation.en: The process of a liquid converting to the gaseous state.

experiment.en: A test under controlled conditions made to either demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the efficacy of something previously untried.

fermentation.en: Any of many anaerobic biochemical reactions in which an enzyme (or several enzymes produced by a microorganism) catalyses the conversion of one substance into another; especially the conversion (using yeast) of sugars to alcohol or acetic acid with the evolution of carbon dioxide

fission.en: The process whereby one item splits to become two.

fusion.en: The act of merging separate elements, or the result thereof.

gene.en: A theoretical unit of heredity of living organisms; a gene may take several values and in principle predetermines a precise trait of an organism's form (phenotype), such as hair color.
gene.ee: A change in a gene is reflected in the protein or RNA molecule that it codes for.

genome.en: The complete genetic information (either DNA or, in some viruses, RNA) of an organism.

geology.en: The science that studies the structure of the earth (or other planets), together with its origin and development, especially by examination of its rocks.

glucose.en: A simple monosaccharide (sugar) with a molecular formula of C6H12O6; it is a principle source of energy for cellular metabolism.

gravity.en: The state or condition of having weight; weight; heaviness.
gravity.ee: I hope you appreciate the gravity of the situation.

half-life.en: The time required for half of the nuclei in a sample of a specific isotope to undergo radioactive decay.

heredity.en: Hereditary transmission of the physical and genetic qualities of parents to their offspring; the biological law by which living beings tend to repeat their characteristics in their descendants.

hydrogen.en: The lightest chemical element (symbol H), with an atomic number of 1 and atomic weight of 1.00794.

inertia.en: The property of a body that resists any change to its uniform motion; equivalent to its mass.

microorganism.en: An organism that is too small to be seen by the unaided eye, especially a single-celled organism, such as a bacterium.
microorganism.ee: The cud is then reswallowed and further digested by specialized microorganisms that live in the rumen.

molecule.en: The smallest particle of a specific element or compound that retains the chemical properties of that element or compound; two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
molecule.ee: Hydrogen chloride is a diatomic molecule, consisting of a hydrogen atom and a chlorine atom.

momentum.en: Of a body in motion: the tendency of a body to maintain its inertial motion; the product of its mass and velocity.

neutron.en: A subatomic particle forming part of the nucleus of an atom and having no charge; it is a combination of an up quark and two down quarks.

nucleus.en: The core, central part of something, around which other elements are assembled.
nucleus.ee: This collection will form the nucleus of a new library.

observation.en: The act of observing, and the fact of being observed (see observance)

orbit.en: A circular or elliptical path of one object around another object, particularly in astronomy and space travel.
orbit.ee: The Moon's orbit around the Earth takes nearly one month to complete.

oxidation.en: The combination of a substance with oxygen.

oxygen.en: The chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994. It is a colorless and odorless gas.

particle.en: A very small piece of matter, a fragment; especially, the smallest possible part of something.

physics.en: A medicine or drug, especially a cathartic or purgative.
physics.ee: Newtonian physics was extended by Einstein to explain the effects of travelling near the speed of light; quantum physics extends it to account for the behaviour of atoms.

planet.en: Each of the seven major bodies which move relative to the fixed stars in the night sky—the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.

polymer.en: A long or larger molecule consisting of a chain or network of many repeating units, formed by chemically bonding together many identical or similar small molecules called monomers. A polymer is formed by polymerization, the joining of many monomer molecules.

predator.en: Any animal or other organism that hunts and kills other organisms (their prey), primarily for food.

prey.en: Anything, as goods, etc., taken or got by violence; anything taken by force from an enemy in war
prey.ee: The rabbit was eaten by the coyote, so the rabbit is the coyote's prey.

proton.en: A positively charged subatomic particle forming part of the nucleus of an atom and determining the atomic number of an element, composed of two up quarks and a down quark.

reaction.en: An action or statement in response to a stimulus or other event.
reaction.ee: The announcement of the verdict brought a violent reaction.

reproduction.en: The act of reproducing new individuals biologically.
reproduction.ee: Unauthorized reproduction of this article is prohibited.

resistance.en: The act of resisting, or the capacity to resist.
resistance.ee: the resistance of bacteria to certain antibiotics

semiconductor.en: A substance with electrical properties intermediate between a good conductor and a good insulator.

solution.en: A homogeneous mixture, which may be liquid, gas or solid, formed by dissolving one or more substances.

spectrum.en: A range; a continuous, infinite, one-dimensional set, possibly bounded by extremes.

symbiosis.en: A relationship of mutual benefit, especially among different species.

temperature.en: A measure of cold or heat, often measurable with a thermometer.
temperature.ee: The temperature in the room dropped nearly 20 degrees; it went from hot to cold.

thermodynamics.en: The science of the conversions between heat and other forms of energy.

universe.en: Our universe, the sum of everything that exists in the cosmos, including time and space itself.
universe.ee: Powerful telescopes look far back into the distant reaches of the Universe.

voltage.en: The difference in electrostatic potential between two points in space, especially between live and neutral conductors or the earth.
voltage.ee: Be careful when opening high-voltage equipment.

zoology.en: The part of biology relating to the animal kingdom, including the structure, embryology, evolution, classification, habits, and distribution of all animals, both living and extinct.

acceleration.en: The act of accelerating, or the state of being accelerated; increase of motion or action; as opposed to retardation or deceleration.
acceleration.ee: a falling body moves toward the earth with an acceleration of velocity

allele.en: One of a number of alternative forms of the same gene occupying a given position, or locus, on a chromosome.

bioluminescence.en: The emission of light by a living organism (such as a firefly).

centrifuge.en: A device in which a mixture of denser and lighter materials (normally dispersed in a liquid) is separated by being spun about a central axis at high speed.

circuit.en: The act of moving or revolving around, or as in a circle or orbit; a revolution

coefficient.en: A constant by which an algebraic term is multiplied.

conduction.en: The conveying of heat or electricity through material.

cross-section.en: A section formed by a plane cutting through an object, usually at right angles to an axis.

decay.en: The process or result of being gradually decomposed.
decay.ee: The pair loved to take pictures in the decaying hospital on forty-third street.

displacement.en: The act of displacing, or the state of being displaced; a putting out of place.

distillation.en: The act of falling in drops, or the act of pouring out in drops.

endothermic.en: Of a chemical reaction that absorbs heat energy from its surroundings.

equilibrium.en: The condition of a system in which competing influences are balanced, resulting in no net change.

ferrite.en: The interstitial solid solution of carbon in body-centered cubic iron.

fractal.en: A mathematical set that has a non-integer and constant Hausdorff dimension; a geometric figure that is self-similar at all scales.

frequency.en: The rate of occurrence of anything; the relationship between incidence and time period.
frequency.ee: The frequency of bus service has been improved from one every 15 to one every 12 minutes.

hydrolysis.en: A chemical process of decomposition involving the splitting of a bond and the addition of the hydrogen cation and the hydroxide anion of water.

immunology.en: The branch of medicine that concerns the body's immune system.

laser.en: A device that produces a monochromatic, coherent beam of light.

lipid.en: Any of a group of organic compounds including the fats, oils, waxes, sterols, and triglycerides. Lipids are characterized by being insoluble in water, and account for most of the fat present in the human body.

meiosis.en: A figure of speech whereby something is made to seem smaller or less important than it actually is; understatement.

microbiology.en: The branch of biology that deals with microorganisms, especially their effects on man and other living organisms.

microscope.en: An optical instrument used for observing small objects.

mitosis.en: The division of a cell nucleus in which the genome is copied and separated into two identical halves. It is normally followed by cell division.

newton.en: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of force; the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram by one metre per second per second. Symbol: N.

nitrate.en: Any salt or ester of nitric acid.

nucleotide.en: The monomer constituting DNA or RNA biopolymer molecules. Each nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous heterocyclic base (or nucleobase), which can be either a double-ringed purine or a single-ringed pyrimidine; a five-carbon pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA or ribose in RNA); and a phosphate group.

optics.en: The physics of light and vision.
optics.ee: The optics of this telescope are particularly good.

phenotype.en: The appearance of an organism based on a multifactorial combination of genetic traits and environmental factors, especially used in pedigrees.

pheromone.en: A chemical secreted by an animal, especially an insect, that affects the development or behavior of other members of the same species, functioning often as a means of attracting a member of the opposite sex.

physiology.en: A branch of biology that deals with the functions and activities of life or of living matter (as organs, tissues, or cells) and of the physical and chemical phenomena involved.

pressure.en: A pressing; a force applied to a surface.
pressure.ee: Apply pressure to the wound to stop the bleeding.

primatology.en: The branch of zoology relating to the study of primates

protist.en: Any of the eukaryotic unicellular organisms including protozoans, slime molds and some algae; historically grouped into the kingdom Protoctista.

radiation.en: The shooting forth of anything from a point or surface, like diverging rays of light.

refraction.en: The turning or bending of any wave, such as a light or sound wave, when it passes from one medium into another of different optical density.

resonance.ee: 2004, When experiments with the first ‘atom-smashers’ took place in the 1950s to 1960s, many short-lived heavier siblings of the proton and neutron, known as ‘resonances’, were discovered. — Frank Close, Particle Physics: A Very Short Introduction (Oxford 2004, p. 35)

respiration.en: The process of inhaling and exhaling; breathing, breath.

sediment.en: A collection of small particles, particularly dirt, that precipitates from a river or other body of water.
sediment.ee: The Nile delta is composed of sediment that was washed down and deposited at the mouth of the river.

sensor.en: A device or organ that detects certain external stimuli and responds in a distinctive manner.

speciation.en: The process by which new distinct species evolve.
speciation.ee: requirements specifying speciation and serotyping in addition to reporting of presence or absence

supernova.en: The explosion of a star, which increases its brightness to typically a billion times that of our sun, though attenuated by the great distance from our sun. Some leave only debris (Type I); others fade to invisibility as neutron stars (Type II).

symbiont.en: An organism that lives in a symbiotic relationship; a symbiote.

toxicology.en: The branch of pharmacology that deals with the nature, effect, detection and treatment of poisons and poisoning.

turbulence.en: The state or fact of being turbulent or agitated; tempestuousness, disturbance.

wavefunction.en: A mathematical function that describes the propagation of the quantum mechanical wave associated with a particle (or system of particles), related to the probability of finding the particle in a particular region of space.

wavelength.en: The length of a single cycle of a wave, as measured by the distance between one peak or trough of a wave and the next; it is often designated in physics as λ, and corresponds to the velocity of the wave divided by its frequency.

acquittal.en: The act of fulfilling the duties (of a given role, obligation etc.).

adjudication.en: The act of adjudicating, of reaching a judgement.

allegation.en: An assertion, especially an accusation, not necessarily based on facts.
allegation.ee: She put forth several allegations regarding her partner in hopes of discrediting his actions.

amendment.en: An alteration or change for the better; correction of a fault or of faults; reformation of life by quitting vices.
amendment.ee: The First Amendment guarantees freedom of religion, speech, press, assembly, and petition.

amnesty.en: Forgetfulness; cessation of remembrance of wrong; oblivion.

appeal.en: An application for the removal of a cause or suit from an inferior to a superior judge or court for re-examination or review.
appeal.ee: He made an appeal for volunteers to help at the festival.

arrest.en: A check, stop, an act or instance of arresting something.
arrest.ee: The police have arrested a suspect in the murder inquiry.

attorney.en: A lawyer; one who advises or represents others in legal matters as a profession.

bail.en: Security, usually a sum of money, exchanged for the release of an arrested person as a guarantee of that person's appearance for trial.
bail.ee: to bail cloth to a tailor to be made into a garment; to bail goods to a carrier

bench.en: A long seat with or without a back, found for example in parks and schools.
bench.ee: They sat on a park bench and tossed bread crumbs to the ducks and pigeons.

bill.en: Any of various bladed or pointed hand weapons, originally designating an Anglo-Saxon sword, and later a weapon of infantry, especially in the 14th and 15th centuries, commonly consisting of a broad, heavy, double-edged, hook-shaped blade, with a short pike at the back and another at the top, attached to the end of a long staff.

compensation.en: The act or principle of compensating.

contract.en: An agreement between two or more parties, to perform a specific job or work order, often temporary or of fixed duration and usually governed by a written agreement.

copyright.en: The right by law to be the entity which determines who may publish, copy and distribute a piece of writing, music, picture or other work of authorship.
copyright.ee: Copyright is a separate legal area from trademarks.

court.en: An enclosed space; a courtyard; an uncovered area shut in by the walls of a building, or by different buildings; also, a space opening from a street and nearly surrounded by houses; a blind alley.
court.ee: The girls were playing in the court.

crime.en: A specific act committed in violation of the law.

custody.en: The legal right to take care of something or somebody, especially children.
custody.ee: The court awarded custody to the child's father.

damages.en: To impair the soundness, goodness, or value of; to harm or cause destruction.
damages.ee: Be careful not to damage any of the fragile items while unpacking them.

decree.ee: A court decrees a restoration of property.

defendant.en: Serving, or suitable, for defense; defensive, defending.

defamation.en: The act of injuring another person's reputation by any slanderous communication, written or oral; the wrong of maliciously injuring the good name of another.

deliberation.en: The act of deliberating, or of weighing and examining the reasons for and against a choice or measure; careful consideration; mature reflection.
deliberation.ee: the deliberations of a legislative body or council

detention.en: The act of detaining or the state of being detained.

discrimination.en: Discernment, the act of discriminating, discerning, distinguishing, noting or perceiving differences between things, with intent to understand rightly and make correct decisions.

dispute.en: An argument or disagreement, a failure to agree.
dispute.ee: Some residents disputed the proposal, saying it was based more on emotion than fact.

duty.en: That which one is morally or legally obligated to do.
duty.ee: We don't have a duty to keep you here.

ethics.en: The study of principles relating to right and wrong conduct.

evidence.en: Facts or observations presented in support of an assertion.
evidence.ee: There is no evidence that anyone was here earlier.

extradition.en: A formal process by which a criminal suspect held by one government is handed over to another government for trial or, if the suspect has already been tried and found guilty, to serve his or her sentence.

felony.en: A serious criminal offense, which, under United States federal law, is punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year or by death.

fine.ee: They filtered silt and fines out of the soil.

fraud.en: The crime of stealing or otherwise illegally obtaining money by use of deception tactics.

guilty.en: A plea by a defendant who does not contest a charge.
guilty.ee: He was guilty of cheating at cards.

hearing.en: (stative) To perceive sounds through the ear.
hearing.ee: I was deaf, and now I can hear.

indictment.en: An official formal accusation for a criminal offence, or the process by which it is brought to a jury.

innocent.en: One who is innocent, especially a young child.
innocent.ee: The slaughter of the innocents was a significant event in the New Testament.

judge.en: A public official whose duty it is to administer the law, especially by presiding over trials and rendering judgments; a justice.
judge.ee: At a boxing match, the decision of the judges is final.

judiciary.en: The collective body of judges, justices, etc.

jurisdiction.en: The power, right, or authority to interpret and apply the law.

jury.en: A group of individuals chosen from the general population to hear and decide a case in a court of law.

justice.en: The state or characteristic of being just or fair.

lawsuit.en: In civil law, a case where two or more people disagree and one or more of the parties take the case to a court for resolution.
lawsuit.ee: The lawyer advised his client against filing a lawsuit as it would take a lot of time and money to resolve.

lawyer.en: A professional person qualified (as by a law degree or bar exam) and authorized to practice law, i.e. represent parties in lawsuits or trials and give legal advice.
lawyer.ee: A lawyer's time and advice are his stock in trade. - aphorism often credited to Abraham Lincoln, but without attestation

legislation.en: The act of legislating; preparation and enactment of laws; the laws enacted.

litigation.ee: That attorney has been chastised for his litigation behavior.

manslaughter.en: The slaying of a human being.

mediation.en: Negotiation to resolve differences conducted by some impartial party.

motive.en: An idea or communication that makes one want to act, especially from spiritual sources; a divine prompting.
motive.ee: No-one could understand why she had hidden the shovel; her motives were obscure at best.

murder.en: The crime of deliberately killing another person without justification.
murder.ee: The defendant was charged with murder.

parole.en: The release of a former prisoner under condition of compliance with specific terms.

penalty.ee: The penalty for his crime was to do hard labor.

plaintiff.en: A party bringing a suit in civil law against a defendant; accusers.

police.en: A civil force granted the legal authority for law enforcement and maintaining public order.

precedent.en: An act in the past which may be used as an example to help decide the outcome of similar instances in the future.

prison.en: A place or institution of confinement, especially of long-term confinement for those convicted of serious crimes or otherwise considered undesirable by the government.
prison.ee: The cold stone walls of the prison had stood for over a century.

prosecutor.ee: Annie Jay was the Wisconsin government prosecutor in the trial of a man for forging his client's signature.

remand.en: The act of sending an accused person back into custody whilst awaiting trial.

reparation.en: (usually in the plural) A payment of time, effort or money to undo past transgression(s).
reparation.ee: the reparation of a bridge or of a highway

rights.en: That which complies with justice, law or reason.
rights.ee: We're on the side of right in this contest.

robbery.en: The act or practice of robbing.

sanction.en: An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.
sanction.ee: The whalers had been operating in the contested waters off the island with sanction from the Japanese government.

sentence.en: The decision or judgement of a jury or court; a verdict.
sentence.ee: The court returned a sentence of guilt in the first charge, but innocence in the second.

slander.en: A false or unsupported, malicious statement (spoken, not written), especially one which is injurious to a person's reputation; the making of such a statement.

sovereign.en: A monarch; the ruler of a country.

suspect.en: A person who is suspected of something, in particular of committing a crime.
suspect.ee: to suspect the presence of disease

testimony.en: Statements made by a witness in court.

trademark.en: A word, symbol, or phrase used to identify a particular company's product and differentiate it from other companies' products.

trial.en: An opportunity to test something out; a test.
trial.ee: They will perform the trials for the new equipment next week.

tribunal.en: An assembly including one or more judges to conduct judicial business; a court of law.

unconstitutional.en: Contrary to or violative of the constitution of a state or other sovereign institution
unconstitutional.ee: That recently passed political bill has been declared unconstitutional.

victim.en: One that is harmed—killed, injured, subjected to oppression, deceived, or otherwise adversely affected—by someone or something, especially another person or event, force, or condition; in particular:
victim.ee: the youngest victims of the brutal war

warrant.en: Authorization or certification; a sanction, as given by a superior.
warrant.ee: a warrant of authenticity; a warrant for success

witness.en: Attestation of a fact or event; testimony.
witness.ee: She can bear witness, since she was there at the time.

authoritarianism.en: A form of government in which the governing body has absolute, or almost absolute, control. Typically this control is maintained by force, and little heed is paid to public opinion or the judicial system.

ballot.en: Originally, a small ball placed in a container to cast a vote; now, by extension, a piece of paper or card used for this purpose, or some other means used to signify a vote.

cabinet.en: A storage closet either separate from, or built into, a wall.

campaign.en: A series of operations undertaken to achieve a set goal.
campaign.ee: The company is targeting children in their latest advertising campaign.

candidate.en: A person who is running in an election.

citizen.en: A resident of a city or town, especially one with legally-recognized rights or duties.
citizen.ee: Diogenes reckoned himself a citizen of the world.

coalition.en: A temporary group or union of organizations, usually formed for a particular advantage.
coalition.ee: The Liberal Democrats and Conservative parties formed a coalition government in 2010.

congress.en: A coming together of two or more people; a meeting.
congress.ee: The National Congress of American Indians

conservative.en: A person who favors maintenance of the status quo.
conservative.ee: The curriculum committee at this university is extremely conservative.

constitution.en: The act, or process of setting something up, or establishing something; the composition or structure of such a thing; its makeup.
constitution.ee: He has a strong constitution, so he should make a quick recovery from the illness.

corruption.en: The act of corrupting or of impairing integrity, virtue, or moral principle; the state of being corrupted or debased; loss of purity or integrity

coup.en: A quick, brilliant, and highly successful act.

democracy.en: Rule by the people, especially as a form of government; either directly or through elected representatives (representative democracy).

dictatorship.en: A type of government where absolute sovereignty is allotted to an individual or a small clique.

diplomat.en: A person, such as an ambassador, who is accredited to represent a government officially in its relations with other governments or international organisations

diplomacy.en: The art and practice of conducting international relations by negotiating alliances, treaties, agreements etc., bilaterally or multilaterally, between states and sometimes international organizations, or even between polities with varying status, such as those of monarchs and their princely vassals.
diplomacy.ee: National diplomacy typically deploys its dexterity to secure advantage for one's nation.

government.en: The body with the power to make and/or enforce laws to control a country, land area, people or organization.
government.ee: If the citizens must follow the law, then the government must follow the constitution.

ideology.en: Doctrine, philosophy, body of beliefs or principles belonging to an individual or group.
ideology.ee: A dictatorship, in order to secure its reign, bans things that do not conform to its ideology.

independence.en: The state or quality of being independent; freedom from dependence; exemption from reliance on, or control by others; self-subsistence or maintenance; direction of one's own affairs without interference.

incumbent.en: The current holder of an office, such as ecclesiastical benefice or an elected office.
incumbent.ee: Proper behavior is incumbent on all holders of positions of trust.

intervention.en: The action of intervening; interfering in some course of events.

isolationism.en: A national (or group) policy of non-interaction with other nations (or groups).
isolationism.ee: Before contact was initiated by the West, China followed a policy of isolationism.

judicial.en: That branch of government which is responsible for maintaining the courts of law and for the administration of justice.

lobbyist.en: A person who is paid to lobby politicians and encourage them to vote a certain way or otherwise use their office to effect a desired result.

manifesto.en: A public declaration of principles, policies, or intentions, especially that of a political party.
manifesto.ee: A creed is a manifesto of religious or spiritual beliefs.

monarchy.en: A government in which sovereignty is embodied within a single, today usually hereditary head of state (whether as a figurehead or as a powerful ruler).

negotiation.en: The process of achieving agreement through discussion.

neoliberalism.en: A political ideology or ideological trend based on neoclassical economics that espouses economic liberalism, favouring trade liberalisation, financial deregulation, a small government, privatisation and liberalisation of government businesses, passive antitrust enforcement, accepting greater economic inequality and disfavouring unionisation.

opposition.en: The action of opposing or of being in conflict.

partisan.en: An adherent to a party or faction.

polling.en: To take, record the votes of (an electorate).
polling.ee: He polled a hundred votes more than his opponent.

power.en: Ability to do or undergo something.

president.en: An act in the past which may be used as an example to help decide the outcome of similar instances in the future.
president.ee: The vast majority of presidents have been male.

ratification.en: The act or process of ratifying, or the state of being ratified.

revolution.en: A political upheaval in a government or nation state characterized by great change.

senate.en: In some bicameral legislative systems, the upper house or chamber.

socialism.en: Any of various economic and political theories advocating collective or governmental ownership and administration of the means of production and distribution of goods.

sovereignty.en: (of a polity) The state of making laws and controlling resources without the coercion of other nations.

state.en: A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time.
state.ee: He stated that he was willing to help.

terrorism.en: The deliberate commission of an act of violence to create public fear through the suffering of the victims in the furtherance of a political or social agenda.

totalitarianism.en: A system of government in which the people have virtually no authority and the state wields absolute control, for example, a dictatorship.

transparency.en: The quality of being transparent; transparence.

tyranny.en: A government in which a single ruler (a tyrant) has absolute power; this system of government.

veto.en: A political right to disapprove of (and thereby stop) the process of a decision, a law etc.

vote.en: A formalized choice on matters of administration or other democratic activities
vote.ee: One occasion indicative votes were used was in 2003 when MPs were presented with seven different options on how to reform the House of Lords.

welfare.en: Health, safety, happiness and prosperity; well-being in any respect.

aesthetics.en: The study or philosophy of beauty.

architecture.en: The art and science of designing and managing the construction of buildings and other structures, particularly if they are well proportioned and decorated.
architecture.ee: Architecture is the visual public expression of a culture’s achievements, values, and outlook. ― Max Roscoe, "How Your City Is Killing You With Ugliness"

artisan.en: A skilled manual worker who uses tools and machinery in a particular craft.

avant-garde.en: The vanguard of an army or other force.
avant-garde.ee: It was a very avant-garde production.

baroque.en: Ornate, intricate, decorated, laden with detail.

biography.en: A person's life story, especially one published.
biography.ee: There are many biographies of Benjamin Franklin.

calligraphy.en: The art or practice of writing letters and words in a decorative style; the letters and words so written.

canvas.en: A type of coarse cloth, woven from hemp, useful for making sails and tents or as a surface for paintings.
canvas.ee: The author takes rural midwestern life as a canvas for a series of tightly woven character studies.

cinema.en: A movie theatre, a movie house
cinema.ee: The cinema is right across the street from the restaurant.

comedy.en: A choric song of celebration or revel, especially in Ancient Greece.
comedy.ee: Why would you be watching comedy when there are kids starving right now?

costume.en: A style of dress, including garments, accessories and hairstyle, especially as characteristic of a particular country, period or people.
costume.ee: The dancer was wearing Highland costume.

cubism.en: (often capitalized) An artistic movement in the early 20th Century characterized by the depiction of natural forms as geometric structures of planes.

dialect.en: A variety of a language that is characteristic of a particular area, community or social group, differing from other varieties of the same language in relatively minor ways as regards grammar, phonology, and lexicon.
dialect.ee: Home computers in the 1980s had many incompatible dialects of BASIC.

documentary.en: A film, TV program, publication etc. which presents a social, political, scientific or historical subject in a factual or informative manner.

drama.en: A composition, normally in prose, telling a story and intended to be represented by actors impersonating the characters and speaking the dialogue

epic.en: An extended narrative poem in elevated or dignified language, celebrating the feats of a deity, demigod (heroic epic), other legend or traditional hero.
epic.ee: The Icelandic epic took all night to recite.

fiction.en: Literary type using invented or imaginative writing, instead of real facts, usually written as prose.
fiction.ee: I am a great reader of fiction.

folklore.en: The tales, legends and superstitions of a particular ethnic population.

gallery.en: An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of works of art.
gallery.ee: a clip-art gallery in a wordprocessor

genre.en: A kind; a stylistic category or sort, especially of literature or other artworks.
genre.ee: The computer game Half-Life redefined the first-person shooter genre.

jazz.en: A musical art form rooted in West African cultural and musical expression and in the African American blues tradition, with diverse influences over time, commonly characterized by blue notes, syncopation, swing, call and response, polyrhythms and improvisation.
jazz.ee: What is all this jazz lying around?

literature.en: The body of all written works.
literature.ee: However, even “literary” science fiction rarely qualifies as literature, because it treats characters as sets of traits rather than as fully realized human beings with unique life stories. —Adam Cadre, 2008

metaphor.en: The use of a word or phrase to refer to something that it is not, invoking a direct similarity between the word or phrase used and the thing described (but in the case of English without the words like or as, since use of those words would imply a simile); the word or phrase used in this way; an implied comparison.

monument.en: A structure built for commemorative or symbolic reasons, or as a memorial; a commemoration.
monument.ee: There is a monument on the town green to the soldiers who died in World War I.

mural.en: A large painting, usually drawn on a wall.

narrative.en: The systematic recitation of an event or series of events.
narrative.ee: The plot is full of holes, but the narrative is extremely compelling.

novel.en: Newly made, formed or evolved; having no precedent; of recent origin; new.

opera.en: A theatrical work, combining drama, music, song and sometimes dance.

originality.en: The quality of being original or novel.

painting.ee: to paint a portrait or a landscape

photography.en: The art and technology of producing images on photosensitive surfaces, and its digital counterpart.

playwright.en: A writer and creator of theatrical plays.

poetry.en: Literature composed in verse or language exhibiting conscious attention to patterns and rhythm.
poetry.ee: That 'Swan Lake' choreography is poetry in motion, fitting the musical poetry of Tchaikovski's divine score well beyond the literary inspiration.

porcelain.en: The plant Smilax china, a liana of much of eastern Asia.
porcelain.ee: He set the table with china, cloth napkins, and crystal stemware.

pottery.en: Fired ceramic wares that contain clay when formed.
pottery.ee: The shelves were lined with pottery of all shapes and sizes.

prose.en: Language, particularly written language, not intended as poetry.
prose.ee: Though known mostly for her prose, she also produced a small body of excellent poems.

satire.en: A literary device of writing or art which principally ridicules its subject often as an intended means of provoking or preventing change. Humor, irony, and exaggeration are often used to aid this.
satire.ee: a stinging satire of American politics.

sketch.en: A rapidly executed freehand drawing that is not intended as a finished work, often consisting of a multitude of overlapping lines.

sonnet.en: A fixed verse form of Italian origin consisting of fourteen lines that are typically five-foot iambics and rhyme according to one of a few prescribed schemes.

storytelling.en: The act and skills of presenting stories and tales.

subculture.en: A portion of a culture distinguished by its customs or other features.
subculture.ee: The goth subculture has its own mode of dress, and it has a characteristic musical style.

symbolism.en: Representation of a concept through symbols or underlying meanings of objects or qualities.

theater.en: A place or building, consisting of a stage and seating, in which an audience gathers to watch plays, musical performances, public ceremonies, and so on.
theater.ee: His grandfather was in the Pacific theater during the war.

theme.en: A subject of a talk or an artistic piece; a topic.
theme.ee: We themed the birthday party around superheroes.

tragedy.en: A drama or similar work, in which the main character is brought to ruin or otherwise suffers the extreme consequences of some tragic flaw or weakness of character.

advertising.en: To give (especially public) notice of (something); to announce publicly.
advertising.ee: For personal needs, advertise on the internet or in a local newspaper.

algorithm.en: A collection of ordered steps that solve a mathematical problem. A precise step-by-step plan for a computational procedure that possibly begins with an input value and yields an output value in a finite number of steps.

anchor.en: A tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of a sea or river to resist movement.

audience.en: A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc.
audience.ee: We joined the audience just as the lights went down.

authenticity.en: The quality of being genuine or not corrupted from the original.
authenticity.ee: I hereby certify the authenticity of this copy.

blog.en: A website that allows users to reflect, share opinions, and discuss various topics in the form of an online journal, sometimes letting readers comment on their posts. Most blogs are written in a slightly informal tone (personal journals, news, businesses, etc.)
blog.ee: This blog was originally posted on my personal site but is reproduced on the forums for greater visibility.

broadcast.en: A transmission of a radio or television programme intended to be received by anyone with a receiver.
broadcast.ee: The DJ was feeling nervous before his first national broadcast.

censorship.en: The use of state or group power to control freedom of expression or press, such as passing laws to prevent media from being published or propagated.

columnist.en: A regular writer of a column, such as in a magazine or newspaper

convergence.en: The act of moving toward union or uniformity.
convergence.ee: We built a homestead at the convergence of two rivers

editorial.en: An article in a publication giving the opinion of its editors on a given topic or current event.

entertainment.en: An activity designed to give pleasure, enjoyment, diversion, amusement, or relaxation to an audience, no matter whether the audience participates passively as in watching opera or a movie, or actively as in games.

gatekeeper.en: A person or group who controls access to something or somebody.

headline.en: The heading or title of a magazine or newspaper article.
headline.ee: The headline on today's newspaper reads "John Doe Wins Wood-Splitting Competition."

magazine.en: A non-academic periodical publication, generally consisting of sheets of paper folded in half and stapled at the fold.

message.en: A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.
message.ee: We've just received an urgent message from the President.

newspaper.en: A publication, usually published daily or weekly and usually printed on cheap, low-quality paper, containing news and other articles.
newspaper.ee: She newspapered one end of the room before painting the bookcase.

objectivity.en: The state of being objective, just, unbiased and not influenced by emotions or personal prejudices.

podcast.en: An audio programme produced on a regular basis, delivered over the Internet in a compressed digital format and designed for playback on computers or portable digital audio players, such as the iPod.

privacy.en: The state of being secluded from the presence, sight, or knowledge of others.
privacy.ee: I need my privacy, so please stay out of my room.

radio.en: The technology that allows for the transmission of sound or other signals by modulation of electromagnetic waves.
radio.ee: I think the boat is sinking; we'd better radio for help. / I radioed him already. / Radio the coordinates this time. / OK. I radioed them the coordinates.

rating.en: To assign or be assigned a particular rank or level.
rating.ee: She is rated fourth in the country.

reporter.ee: The reporters of important security bugs may be paid a bounty by the software developer.

sensationalism.en: The use of sensational subject matter, style or methods, or the sensational subject matter itself; behavior, published materials, or broadcasts that are intentionally controversial, exaggerated, lurid, loud, or attention-grabbing. subscription.en: Access to a resource for a period of time, generally for payment.
subscription.ee: I have a monthly subscription to the Daily Telegraph newspaper.

television.en: An electronic communication medium that allows the transmission of real-time visual images, and often sound.
television.ee: It’s a good thing that television doesn’t transmit smell.

trending.en: To have a particular direction; to run; to stretch; to tend.
trending.ee: The shore of the sea trends to the southwest.

viral.en: A video, image or text spread by "word of mouth" on the internet or by e-mail for humorous, political or marketing purposes.

vlog.en: A weblog using video as its primary presentation format.

agile.en: Having the faculty of quick motion in the limbs; apt or ready to move

benchmarking.en: To measure the performance or quality of (an item) relative to another similar item in an impartial scientific manner.

brand.ee: To burn something to brands and ashes.

breakeven.en: To neither gain nor lose money.

budget.en: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or time-frame.

collaboration.ee: Collaboration can be a useful part of the creative process.

consultant.en: A person or party that is consulted

decision-making.en: The process of reaching a decision.

executive.en: A chief officer or administrator, especially one who can make significant decisions on their own authority.

hr.en: A time period of sixty minutes; one twenty-fourth of a day.

inventory.en: (operations) The stock of an item on hand at a particular location or business.

leadership.en: The capacity of someone to lead others.

logistics.en: A logistic function or graph of a logistic curve.

management.en: Administration; the use of limited resources combined with forecasting, planning, leadership and execution skills to achieve predetermined specific goals.

networking.en: To interact socially for the purpose of getting connections or personal advancement.
networking.ee: Many people find it worthwhile to network for jobs and information.

offshore.en: An area or or portion of sea away from the shore.

pipeline.en: A conduit made of pipes used to convey water, gas or petroleum etc.

pitch.en: A sticky, gummy substance secreted by trees; sap.
pitch.ee: It is hard to get this pitch off my hand.

procurement.en: The purchasing department of a company.

profitability.en: The quality or state of being profitable; capacity to make a profit.

recruitment.en: The process or art of finding candidates for a post in an organization, or recruits for the armed forces.

sales.ee: He celebrated after the sale of company.

stakeholder.en: A person holding the stakes of bettors, with the responsibility of delivering the pot to the winner of the bet.

startup.en: The act or process of starting a process or machine.

strategy.en: The science and art of military command as applied to the overall planning and conduct of warfare.

venture.en: A risky or daring undertaking or journey.

vision.en: The sense or ability of sight.
vision.ee: He tried drinking from the pool of water, but realized it was only a vision.

brownfield.en: A site, to be used for housing or commerce, that has been previously used for industry and may be contaminated or need extensive clearing

congestion.en: The hindrance or blockage of the passage of something, for example a fluid, mixture, traffic, people, etc. (due to an excess of this or due to a partial or complete obstruction), resulting in overfilling or overcrowding.

downtown.en: The main business part of a city or town, usually located at or near its center.
downtown.ee: John walked every day to his downtown job.

neighborhood.en: The quality of being a neighbor, of living nearby, next to each-other; proximity.
neighborhood.ee: Our neighborhood was our only reason to exchange hollow greetings.

suburb.en: A residential area located on the outskirts of a city or large town that usually includes businesses that cater to its residents; such as schools, grocery stores, shopping centers, restaurants, convenience stores, etc.

corridor.en: A narrow hall or passage with rooms leading off it, as in a building or in a railway carriage.

park.en: An area of land set aside for environment preservation or recreation.
park.ee: A country's tank park or artillery park.

parking.en: To bring (something such as a vehicle) to a halt or store in a specified place.
parking.ee: I parked the drive heads of my hard disk before travelling with my laptop.

pedestrian.en: A walker; one who walks or goes on foot, especially as opposed to one who uses a vehicle.

redevelopment.en: The process of developing something anew.
redevelopment.ee: the redevelopment of the hero's character in a comic book

residential.en: A trip during which people temporarily live together.
residential.ee: The youth group organises annual residentials.

segregation.en: The setting apart or separation of things or people, as a natural process, a manner of organizing people that may be voluntary or enforced by law.

slum.en: A dilapidated neighborhood where many people live in a state of poverty.

aquaculture.en: The cultivation of aquatic produce such as aquatic plants, fish and other aquatic animals.

calorie.en: (nutrition) Kilogram calorie or large calorie. A unit of energy 1000 times larger than the gram calorie. It is equivalent to the gram kilocalorie, approximately 4.2 kilojoules.

carbohydrate.en: (nutrition) A sugar, starch, or cellulose that is a food source of energy for an animal or plant.
carbohydrate.ee: These microbes are primarily responsible for breaking down cellulose and other carbohydrates into volatile fatty acids (VFAs).

fallow.en: Ground ploughed and harrowed but left unseeded for one year.
fallow.ee: a fallow period in one's career

fertilizer.en: A natural substance that is used to make the ground more suitable for growing plants.

grain.en: The harvested seeds of various grass food crops eg: wheat, corn, barley.
grain.ee: We stored a thousand tons of grain for the winter.

harvest.en: The third season of the year; autumn; fall.
harvest.ee: Harvest is usually very damp and rainy.

horticulture.en: The art or science of cultivating gardens; gardening.

hunger.en: A need or compelling desire for food.
hunger.ee: I have a hunger to win.

hydroponics.en: The cultivation of plants in a nutrient solution rather than in the soil.

livestock.en: Farm animals; animals domesticated for cultivation.

locavore.en: One who tries to eat only locally grown foods.

nutrient.en: A source of nourishment, such as food, that can be metabolized by an organism to give energy and build tissue.

permaculture.en: Any system of sustainable agriculture that renews natural resources and enriches local ecosystems.

smallholder.en: A person who owns or runs a smallholding.
