Because small slaveholders aspired to be planters, they did not often align themselves with the political and economic interests of nonslaveholders." (Wilma P. Dunaway, Slavery in the American Mountain South: "Introduction" 9, 2003)

undernutrition.en: Inadequate nutrition, either due to a lack of food, or to the inability of the body to absorb its nutrients

weed.en: Any plant regarded as unwanted at the place where, and at the time when it is growing.
weed.ee: If it isn't in a straight line or marked with a label, it's a weed.

yield.en: To pay, give in payment; repay, recompense; reward; requite.
yield.ee: Yield the right of way to pedestrians.

aggression.en: The act of initiating hostilities or invasion.

attachment.en: The act or process of (physically or figuratively) attaching.
attachment.ee: I have such an attachment towards my fiancé!

attribution.ee: The attribution of the quote is widely regarded as dubious.

conditioning.en: To subject to the process of acclimation.
conditioning.ee: I became conditioned to the absence of seasons in San Diego.

consciousness.en: The state of being conscious or aware; awareness.

denial.ee: The denial of "There might be X" is the null, "False, there is no X."

ego.en: The self, especially with a sense of self-importance.

empathy.en: Identification with or understanding of the thoughts, feelings, or emotional state of another person.
empathy.ee: She had a lot of empathy for her neighbor; she knew what it was like to lose a parent too.

memory.en: The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later at will.
memory.ee: Memory is a facility common to all animals.

obedience.ee: Obedience is essential in any army.

optimism.en: A tendency to expect the best, or at least, a favourable outcome
optimism.ee: I love her youth, her beauty and above all her optimism that everything will turn out fine.

paranoia.en: A psychotic disorder characterized by delusions of persecution, conspiracy and perceived threat against the person, often associated with false accusations and general mistrust of others

perception.en: The organisation, identification and interpretation of sensory information.

projection.en: Something which projects, protrudes, juts out, sticks out, or stands out.
projection.ee: The face of the cliff had many projections that were big enough for birds to nest on.

rationalization.en: The process, or result of rationalizing.

repression.en: The act of repressing; state of being repressed.
repression.ee: History shows that when governments fear the truth and increase repression, their days are limited.

reward.en: Something of value given in return for an act.
reward.ee: For catching the thief, you'll get a nice reward.

schema.en: An outline or image universally applicable to a general conception, under which it is likely to be presented to the mind (for example, a body schema).

shaping.ee: Earth was shapen by God for God's folk.

stereotype.en: A conventional, formulaic, and often oversimplified or exaggerated conception, opinion, or image of (a person).

stimulus.en: Any external phenomenon that has an influence on a system, by triggering or modifying an internal phenomenon.

subconscious.en: That part of the mind that is not consciously perceived; one's innermost thoughts.
subconscious.ee: A person can sometimes wake up knowing the solution to a problem that their subconscious has been working on.

superego.en: The part of the mind that acts as a self-critical conscience, reflecting social standards that have been learnt.

trauma.en: Any serious injury to the body, often resulting from violence or an accident.

unconscious.ee: After the anesthetist administered the general anesthetic the patient was unconscious.

vulnerability.en: Susceptibility to attack or injury; the state or condition of being weak or poorly defended.
vulnerability.ee: The country recognized their defence vulnerability after an airplane landed in front of the central square without any consequences.

accommodation.en: (usually a mass noun) Lodging in a dwelling or similar living quarters afforded to travellers in hotels or on cruise ships, or prisoners, etc.

agritourism.en: A form of tourism in which tourists stay in farms or agricultural villages, either to experience farm life, or as a base for exploring the countryside

airline.en: A company that flies airplanes to transport people and goods.

airport.en: An airfield (an area designated for the takeoff and landing of aircraft), including one or more runways and (for commercial airports) one or more passenger terminals.
airport.ee: Because of this, and contrary to popular belief, British airports primarily act as giant wealth extractors, transporting our richest citizens out of the country as often as possible to take their money overseas. ― The Independent, Heathrow expansion to mainly benefit wealthy frequent fliers, research finds, 23 june 2018.

customs.en: (in the plural) The duties or taxes imposed on imported or exported goods.
customs.ee: Customs of £200 were due on all the wine we took back from France.

destination.en: The act of destining or appointing.

emigration.en: The act of emigrating; movement of a person or persons out of a country or national region, for the purpose of permanent relocation of residence.

excursion.en: A brief recreational trip; a journey out of the usual way.
excursion.ee: While driving home I took an excursion and saw some deer.

expedition.en: The act of expediting something; prompt execution.

fare.en: A going; journey; travel; voyage; course; passage.

ferry.en: A ship used to transport people, smaller vehicles and goods from one port to another, usually on a regular schedule.
ferry.ee: Trucks plowed through the water to ferry flood victims to safety.

flight.ee: Most birds are capable of flight.

guesthouse.en: A small house near a main house, for lodging visitors.

hotel.en: A large town house or mansion; a grand private residence, especially in France.

immigration.en: The act of immigrating; the passing or coming into a country of which one is not native born for the purpose of permanent residence.

itinerary.en: A written schedule of activities for a vacation or road trip.

layover.en: A break between stages of a journey.
layover.ee: We had a layover while waiting to change planes, so we stretched our legs.

luggage.en: The bags and other containers that hold a traveller's belongings.

migration.en: An instance of moving to live in another place for a while.
migration.ee: The migration of lead from a can to the food inside it can cause lead poisoning.

passport.en: An official document normally used for international journeys, which proves the identity and nationality of the person for whom it was issued.
passport.ee: You will have to bring your passport to prove who you are.

pilgrimage.en: A journey made to a sacred place, or a religious journey.
pilgrimage.ee: In the Muslim faith, the pilgrimage to Mecca is known as the Hajj.

resort.en: A place where people go for recreation, especially one with facilities such as lodgings, entertainment, and a relaxing environment.

sightseeing.en: To go sightseeing; to visit places of interest in a city, town or geographical area.
sightseeing.ee: Sightseeing is a frequent reason to visit San Francisco.

souvenir.en: An item of sentimental value, to remember an event or location.

transit.en: The act of passing over, across, or through something.
transit.ee: the transit of goods through a country

trekking.en: To make a slow or arduous journey.

vacation.en: Freedom from some business or activity.
vacation.ee: The Conservative Party’s vacation of the centre ground gave an opportunity to its opponents.

visa.en: A permit to enter and leave a country, normally issued by the authorities of the country to be visited.

aerobics.en: A form of exercise, designed to enhance one's cardiovascular fitness, normally performed to music.

amateur.ee: The contest is only open to amateurs.

athlete.en: A participant in a group of sporting activities which includes track and field, road running, cross country running and racewalking.
athlete.ee: She's the first athlete in her sport to obtain a corporate sponsor.

athletics.en: (especially Britain) A group of sporting activities including track and field, road running, cross country and racewalking.

badminton.en: A racquet sport played indoors on a court by two opposing players (singles) or two opposing pairs of players (doubles), in which a shuttlecock is volleyed over a net and the competitions are presided by an umpire in British English and a referee in American English.

balance.en: A state in which opposing forces harmonise; equilibrium.
balance.ee: Blair thought he could provide a useful balance to Bush's policies.

basketball.en: A sport in which two opposing teams of five players strive to put a ball through a hoop.

championship.en: A competition to determine a champion, especially the final of a series of competitions.
championship.ee: His championship of civil rights eventually bore fruit.

endurance.en: The measure of a person's stamina or persistence.
endurance.ee: He has great endurance: he ran a marathon and then cycled home.

fencing.en: To enclose, contain or separate by building fence.
fencing.ee: Fencing was erected around the field to keep the horses in.

fitness.en: The condition of being fit, suitable or appropriate.

flexibility.en: The quality of being flexible; suppleness; pliability.
flexibility.ee: I had some flexibility in terms of whether to stay in a hotel or in a bed-and-breakfast.

football.en: (general) A sport played on foot in which teams attempt to get a ball into a goal or zone defended by the other team.
football.ee: Roman and medieval football matches were more violent than any modern type of football.

muscle.en: A contractile form of tissue which animals use to effect movement.
muscle.ee: Muscle consists largely of actin and myosin filaments.

referee.en: An umpire or judge; an official who makes sure the rules are followed during a game.
referee.ee: The referee kicked Jim out of the game for fighting.

rowing.en: To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
rowing.ee: to row the captain ashore in his barge

swimming.en: The act or art of sustaining and propelling the body in water.

tennis.en: A sport played by two players (or four in doubles), who alternately strike the ball over a net using racquets.

volleyball.en: A game played on a rectangular court between two teams of two to six players which involves striking a ball back and forth over a net.

wellness.en: The quality or state of being in good health.

yoga.en: Any of several Hindu or Buddhist disciplines aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquillity; especially a system of exercises practiced to promote control of the body and mind.

anthropology.en: The holistic scientific and social study of humanity, mainly using ethnography as its method.
anthropology.ee: According to anthropology, there are six basic patterns of kinship terminology (i.e., "kin naming systems"): Sudanese, Hawaiian, Eskimo, Crow, Omaha, and Iroquois.

autonomy.en: Self-government; freedom to act or function independently.

dignity.en: The state of being dignified or worthy of esteem: elevation of mind or character.

fairness.en: The property of being fair or equitable.
fairness.ee: Some questioned the fairness of the new laws.

fallacy.en: Deceptive or false appearance; that which misleads the eye or the mind.

freedom.en: The state of being free, of not being imprisoned or enslaved.
freedom.ee: Having recently been released from prison, he didn't know what to do with his newfound freedom.

idealism.en: The property of a person of having high ideals that are usually unrealizable or at odds with practical life.

individualism.en: The tendency for a person to act without reference to others, particularly in matters of style, fashion or mode of thought.

logic.en: A method of human thought that involves thinking in a linear, step-by-step manner about how a problem can be solved. Logic is the basis of many principles including the scientific method.
logic.ee: It's hard to work out his system of logic.

materialism.en: Constant concern over material possessions and wealth; a great or excessive regard for worldly concerns.

morality.en: Recognition of the distinction between good and evil or between right and wrong; respect for and obedience to the rules of right conduct; the mental disposition or characteristic of behaving in a manner intended to produce morally good results.

nihilism.en: (usually uncountable) The view that all endeavours are devoid of objective meaning.

phenomenology.en: The study of structures of consciousness as experienced from the first-person point of view.

philosophy.ee: Philosophy is often divided into five major branches: logic, metaphysics, epistemology, ethics and aesthetics.

pragmatism.en: The pursuit of practicality over aesthetic qualities; a concentration on facts rather than emotions or ideals.

stoicism.en: A school of philosophy popularized during the Roman Empire that emphasized reason as a means of understanding the natural state of things, or logos, and as a means of freeing oneself from emotional distress.

assert.en: An assertion; a section of source code which tests whether an expected condition is true.
assert.ee: He would often assert that there was life on other planets.

drawback.en: A disadvantage; something that detracts or takes away.
drawback.ee: Poor fuel economy is a common drawback among larger vehicles.

far-reaching.en: Having a broad range, scope, or influence.

however.en: Nevertheless; yet, still; in spite of (that).
however.ee: He told me not to do it. I, however, did it anyway. / I did it anyway, however. / (sometimes proscribed:) However, I did it anyway.

indisputable.en: Not disputable; not open to question; obviously true

largely.en: In a widespread or large manner.
largely.ee: They were largely successful in their efforts.

mitigate.en: To reduce, lessen, or decrease; to make less severe or easier to bear.

moreover.en: In addition to what has been said; furthermore; additionally.

necessarily.ee: It is not necessarily true that children get their morals from their parents.

nevertheless.en: In spite of what preceded; yet.

notwithstanding.en: An instance of the word "notwithstanding", often characteristic of legalese.
notwithstanding.ee: He, notwithstanding, persisted in his inquiries.

outweigh.en: To exceed in weight or mass.

paramount.ee: Getting those credit cards paid off is paramount.

primarily.en: (focus) Of a primary or central nature, first and foremost

proponent.en: One who supports something; an advocate

tackle.en: A device for grasping an object and an attached means of moving it, as a rope and hook.
tackle.ee: The government's measures to tackle crime were insufficient.

unless.en: Except on a specified condition; if not.
unless.ee: I’m leaving unless I get a pay rise (AmE: raise).

well-established.en: Having been established for a long period of time.
well-established.ee: The school has a number of well-established traditions.

whereas.en: A clause, as in legal documents, stating whereas.
whereas.ee: He came first in the race, whereas his brother came last.

anomaly.en: A deviation from a rule or from what is regarded as normal; an outlier.
anomaly.ee: He is an anomaly among his friends in that he's the only one who's unmarried.

assertion.en: The act of asserting; positive declaration or averment.
assertion.ee: You're a man of strong assertions!

assumption.en: The act of assuming, or taking to or upon oneself; the act of taking up or adopting.
assumption.ee: His assumption of secretarial duties was timely.

claim.en: A demand of ownership made for something.

concede.en: To yield or suffer; to surrender; to grant
concede.ee: He conceded the race once it was clear he could not win.

confine.en: (chiefly in the plural) A boundary or limit.

contend.en: To strive in opposition; to contest; to dispute; to vie; to quarrel; to fight.
contend.ee: In this paper the author contends that no useful results can be obtained if this method is used.

corroborate.en: To confirm or support something with additional evidence; to attest or vouch for.

counterpart.en: Either of two parts that fit together, or complement one another.
counterpart.ee: Those brass knobs and their hollow counterparts interlock perfectly

detract.en: To take away; to withdraw or remove.

discern.en: To detect with the senses, especially with the eyes.
discern.ee: He was too young to discern right from wrong.

discourse.ee: The preacher gave us a long discourse on duty.

dismiss.en: To discharge; to end the employment or service of.
dismiss.ee: The company dismissed me after less than a year.

disparity.en: The state of being unequal; difference.

distinction.en: That which distinguishes; a single occurrence of a determining factor or feature, the fact of being divided; separation, discrimination.
distinction.ee: There is a distinction to be made between resting and slacking.

embed.en: An embedded reporter or journalist, such as a war reporter assigned to and travelling with a military unit, or a political reporter assigned to follow and report on the campaign of a candidate.
embed.ee: to embed something in clay, mortar, or sand

embody.en: To represent in a physical or concrete form; to incarnate or personify.
embody.ee: As the car salesman approached, wearing a plaid suit and slicked-back hair, he seemed to embody sleaze.

emphasize.en: To stress, give emphasis or extra weight to (something).

endorse.en: A diminutive of the pale, usually appearing in pairs on either side of a pale.

enumerate.en: To specify each member of a sequence individually in incrementing order.

evolve.en: To move in regular procession through a system.

exacerbate.en: To make worse (a problem, bad situation, negative feeling, etc.); aggravate; exasperate.
exacerbate.ee: The proposed shutdown would exacerbate unemployment problems.

exemplify.en: To show or illustrate by example.

exhibit.ee: The museum's new exhibit is drawing quite a crowd.

fluctuate.ee: I fluctuated between wishing he was back home and wishing I'd never met him.

formulate.en: To reduce to, or express in, a formula; to put in a clear and definite form of statement or expression.

generalize.en: To speak in generalities, or in vague terms.

hinder.en: To make difficult to accomplish; to act as an obstacle; to frustrate.
hinder.ee: A drought hinders the growth of plants.

impetus.en: Something that impels; a stimulating factor.
impetus.ee: The outbreak of World War II in 1939 gave a new impetus to receiver development.

inclined.en: To bend or move (something) out of a given plane or direction, often the horizontal or vertical.
inclined.ee: He had to incline his body against the gusts to avoid being blown down in the storm.

inhibit.en: To hold in or hold back; to keep in check; restrain.

insight.en: A sight or view of the interior of anything; a deep inspection or view; introspection; frequently used with into.

intricate.en: Having a great deal of fine detail or complexity.
intricate.ee: The architecture of this clock is very intricate.

invoke.en: To call upon (a person, a god) for help, assistance or guidance.
invoke.ee: The envoy invoked the King of Kings's magnanimity to reduce his province's tribute after another drought.

jeopardize.en: To put in jeopardy, to threaten.
jeopardize.ee: After having an affair with a junior, her chances of promotion were seriously jeopardized.

landmark.en: An object that marks the boundary of a piece of land (usually a stone, or a tree).

legitimate.en: A person born to a legally married couple.
legitimate.ee: legitimate reasoning; a legitimate standard or method

limitation.en: The act of limiting or the state of being limited.
limitation.ee: Getting into his wheelchair after his amputation, it felt like a limitation you could roll in.

manifest.en: A list or invoice of the passengers or goods being carried by a commercial vehicle or ship.
manifest.ee: His courage manifested itself through the look on his face.

marginalize.en: To relegate (something, especially a topic or a group of people) to the margins or to a lower limit; to exclude socially or otherwise.

obscure.en: To render obscure; to darken; to make dim; to keep in the dark; to hide; to make less visible, intelligible, legible, glorious, beautiful, or illustrious.
obscure.ee: an obscure passage or inscription;    The speaker made obscure references to little-known literary works.

paradox.en: An apparently self-contradictory statement, which can only be true if it is false, and vice versa.
paradox.ee: "This sentence is false" is a paradox.

pervasive.en: Manifested throughout; pervading, permeating, penetrating or affecting everything.
pervasive.ee: The medication had a pervasive effect on the patient's health.

pivotal.en: Of, relating to, or being a pivot.

postulate.en: Something assumed without proof as being self-evident or generally accepted, especially when used as a basis for an argument. Sometimes distinguished from axioms as being relevant to a particular science or context, rather than universally true, and following from other axioms rather than being an absolute assumption.

premise.en: A proposition antecedently supposed or proved; something previously stated or assumed as the basis of further argument; a condition; a supposition.

rebut.en: To drive back or beat back; to repulse.

refute.en: To prove (something) to be false or incorrect.

repercussion.en: A consequence or ensuing result of some action.
repercussion.ee: You realize this little stunt of yours is going to have some pretty serious repercussions.

scrutinize.en: To examine something with great care or detail, as to look for hidden or obscure flaws.
scrutinize.ee: to scrutinize the conduct or motives of individuals

substantiate.en: To verify something by supplying evidence; to authenticate or corroborate

supersede.en: An updated newsgroup post that supersedes an earlier version.

tentative.en: A trial; an experiment; an attempt.

trace.ee: Your cell phone company can put a trace on your line.

transform.en: An operation (often an integration) that converts one function into another.
transform.ee: The alchemists sought to transform lead into gold.

undermine.en: To dig underneath (something), to make a passage for destructive or military purposes; to sap.
undermine.ee: The war efforts were undermined by the constant bickering between the allies.

viable.en: An organism that is able to live and develop.

widespread.en: Affecting a large area (e.g. the entire land or body); broad in extent; widely diffused.

citizenship.en: The status of being a citizen, in its various senses.

community.en: A group sharing a common understanding, and often the same language, law, manners, and/or tradition.

culture.en: The arts, customs, lifestyles, background, and habits that characterize a particular society or nation.
culture.ee: I'm headed to the lab to make sure my cell culture hasn't died.

gender.ee: The effect of the medication is dependent upon age, gender, and other factors.

integration.en: The act or process of making whole or entire.

law.en: The body of binding rules and regulations, customs and standards established in a community by its legislative and judicial authorities.

poverty.en: The quality or state of being poor; lack of money

racism.en: Belief that there are distinct human races with inherent differences which determine their abilities, and generally that some are superior and others inferior.
racism.ee: Martin Luther King spoke out against racism.

refugee.en: A person seeking refuge in a foreign country out of fear of political persecution or the prospect of such persecution in their home country, i.e., a person seeking political asylum.

religion.en: Belief in a spiritual or metaphysical reality (often including at least one deity), accompanied by practices or rituals pertaining to the belief.
religion.ee: My brother tends to value religion, but my sister not as much.

society.en: A long-standing group of people sharing cultural aspects such as language, dress, norms of behavior and artistic forms.
society.ee: This society has been known for centuries for its colorful clothing and tight-knit family structure.

tradition.en: A part of culture that is passed from person to person or generation to generation, possibly differing in detail from family to family, such as the way to celebrate holidays.

urbanisation.en: The process of the formation and growth of cities

cohesion.en: State of cohering, or of working together.
cohesion.ee: Unit cohesion is important in the military.

collective.en: A farm owned by a collection of people
collective.ee: the collective body of a nation

conflict.en: A clash or disagreement, often violent, between two or more opposing groups or individuals.
conflict.ee: The conflict between the government and the rebels began three years ago.

consensus.en: A process of decision-making that seeks widespread agreement among group members.
consensus.ee: After years of debate over the best wine to serve at Thanksgiving, no real consensus has emerged.

ethnicity.en: The common characteristics of a group of people, especially regarding ancestry, culture, language or national experiences.

governance.en: The process, or the power, of governing; government or administration.

homogeneous.en: Of the same kind; alike, similar.

inclusion.en: An addition or annex to a group, set, or total.
inclusion.ee: The poem was a new inclusion in the textbook.

marginalised.en: To relegate (something, especially a topic or a group of people) to the margins or to a lower limit; to exclude socially or otherwise.

mobility.en: The ability to move; capacity for movement.

privilege.en: (ecclesiastical law) An exemption from certain laws granted by the Pope.
privilege.ee: All first-year professors here must teach four courses a term, yet you're only teaching one! What entitled you to such a privilege?

protest.en: A formal objection, especially one by a group.
protest.ee: They lodged a protest with the authorities.

representation.ee: The Venus of Willendorf was an early representation of the female body.

solidarity.en: A bond of unity or agreement between individuals, united around a common goal or against a common enemy, such as the unifying principle that defines the labor movement; mutual support within a group.
solidarity.ee: A long time union member himself, Phil showed solidarity with the picketing grocery store workers by shopping at a competing, unionized store.

vulnerable.en: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
vulnerable.ee: It's okay to get vulnerable every now and again.

assimilation.en: The act of assimilating or the state of being assimilated.

demographic.en: (chiefly in plural) A demographic criterion: a characteristic used to classify people for statistical purposes, such as age, race, or gender.

ethnocentrism.en: The tendency to look at the world primarily from the perspective of one's own traditional, deferred, or adoptive ethnic culture.

intersectionality.en: The quality or state of being intersectional, that is, of being characterized by intersection (especially of multiple forms of discrimination).
intersectionality.ee: the intersectionality of gender, class, ethnicity, age, generation, marital status, and place of origin

normative.en: Of or pertaining to a norm or standard.

automation.en: The act or process of converting the controlling of a machine or device to a more automatic system, such as computer or electronic controls.

bandwidth.en: The width, usually measured in hertz, of a frequency band.
bandwidth.ee: I think it's a worthy project, but I just don't have the bandwidth right now.

data.en: (plural: data) A measurement of something on a scale understood by both the recorder (a person or device) and the reader (another person or device). The scale is arbitrarily defined, such as from 1 to 10 by ones, 1 to 100 by 0.1, or simply true or false, on or off, yes, no, or maybe, etc.

database.en: (general) A collection of (usually) organized information in a regular structure, usually but not necessarily in a machine-readable format accessible by a computer.
database.ee: I have a database of all my contacts in my personal organizer.

digital.ee: He moved to digital for the first time, using a Sony camera.

hardware.en: Fixtures, equipment, tools and devices used for general-purpose construction and repair of a structure or object. Also such equipment as sold as stock by a store of the same name, e.g. hardware store.

network.en: A fabric or structure of fibrous elements attached to each other at regular intervals.
network.ee: A network of roads crisscrossed the country.

platform.en: A raised stage from which speeches are made and on which musical and other performances are made.
platform.ee: This new talk show will give a platform to everyday men and women.

programming.en: To enter a program or other instructions into (a computer or other electronic device) to instruct it to do a particular task.
programming.ee: He programmed the DVR to record his favorite show.

robot.en: A machine built to carry out some complex task or group of tasks by physically moving, especially one which can be programmed.

software.en: Encoded computer instructions, usually modifiable (unless stored in some form of unalterable memory such as ROM).

surveillance.en: Close observation of an individual or group; person or persons under suspicion.

wireless.ee: Only about a hundred years ago, wireless was a new technology.

autonomous.en: Self-governing. Intelligent, sentient, self-aware, thinking, feeling, governing independently.

blockchain.en: A shared record of past transactions in a cryptocurrency network.

hacking.en: To chop or cut down in a rough manner.
hacking.ee: They hacked the brush down and made their way through the jungle.

interface.en: The point of interconnection or contact between entities.
interface.ee: Public relations firms often serve as the interface between a company and the press.

microprocessor.en: The entire CPU of a computer on a single integrated circuit (chip).

optimisation.en: The design and operation of a system or process to make it as good as possible in some defined sense.

prototype.en: An original form or object which is a basis for other forms or objects (particularly manufactured items), or for its generalizations and models.
prototype.ee: The prototype had loose wires and rough edges, but it worked.

wearable.en: Something that can be worn; an item of clothing.

adversarial.en: Characteristic of, or in the manner of, an adversary; combative, hostile, opposed

cryptography.en: The discipline concerned with communication security (eg, confidentiality of messages, integrity of messages, sender authentication, non-repudiation of messages, and many other related issues), regardless of the used medium such as pencil and paper or computers.

decentralisation.en: The action of decentralizing, or the state of being decentralized.

able.ee: I’ll see you as soon as I’m able.

about.ee: After my bout with Guillan-Barre Syndrome, it took me 6 months to be up and about again.

above.ee: He's in a better place now, floating free as the clouds above.

accept.en: To receive, especially with a consent, with favour, or with approval.
accept.ee: The Boy Scouts were going to accept him as a member.

according.en: To make to agree or correspond; to suit one thing to another; to adjust.
according.ee: This according voice of national wisdom.

account.en: A registry of pecuniary transactions; a written or printed statement of business dealings or debts and credits, and also of other things subjected to a reckoning or review.
account.ee: to keep one's account at the bank.

across.en: (crosswords, often in combination) A word that runs horizontally in the completed puzzle grid or its associated clue.
across.ee: I solved all of the acrosses, but then got stuck on 3 down.

action.en: Something done so as to accomplish a purpose.
action.ee: Knead bread with a rocking action.

add.en: An act or instance of adding.
add.ee: When the player has fought the boss for one minute, two adds will arrive from the back and must be dealt with.

adult.en: A fully grown human or animal.
adult.ee: an adult human, animal, or plant

after.en: Later; second (of two); next, following, subsequent
after.ee: The after gun is abaft the forward gun.

age.en: The whole duration of a being, whether animal, plant, or other kind, being alive.

ago.en: Gone; gone by; gone away; passed; passed away.

all.en: (with a possessive pronoun) Everything that one is capable of.
all.ee: She gave her all, and collapsed at the finish line.

allow.en: To grant, give, admit, accord, afford, or yield; to let one have.
allow.ee: to allow a servant his liberty;  to allow a free passage;  to allow one day for rest

almost.en: Something or someone that doesn't quite make it.
almost.ee: In all the submissions, they found four papers that were clearly worth publishing and another dozen almosts.

alone.ee: I can't ask for help because I am alone.

along.ee: John played the piano and everyone sang along.

already.en: Prior to some specified time, either past, present, or future; by this time; previously.

also.en: (focus) In addition; besides; as well; further; too.
also.ee: They had porridge for breakfast, and also toast.

although.en: Though, even though, in spite of or despite the fact that: introducing a clause that expresses a concession.
although.ee: Although it was very muddy, the football game went on.

always.en: At all times; throughout all time; since the beginning.
always.ee: Airplanes did not always exist as a form of transportation.

among.en: Denotes a mingling or intermixing with distinct or separable objects. (See Usage Note at amidst.)
among.ee: How can you speak with authority about their customs when you have never lived among them?

amount.en: The total, aggregate or sum of material (not applicable to discrete numbers or units or items in standard English).
amount.ee: The amount of atmospheric pollution threatens a health crisis.

animal.en: In scientific usage, a multicellular organism that is usually mobile, whose cells are not encased in a rigid cell wall (distinguishing it from plants and fungi) and which derives energy solely from the consumption of other organisms (distinguishing it from plants).
animal.ee: A cat is an animal, not a plant. Humans are also animals, under the scientific definition, as we are not plants.

another.en: An additional one of the same kind.
another.ee: There is one sterling and here is another

answer.en: A response or reply; something said or done in reaction to a statement or question.
answer.ee: Her answer to his proposal was a slap in the face.

any.en: To even the slightest extent, at all.
any.ee: I will not remain here any longer.

anyone.ee: Almost anyone can change a light bulb.

appear.en: To come or be in sight; to be in view; to become visible.
appear.ee: A great writer appeared at that time.

arm.en: The portion of the upper human appendage, from the shoulder to the wrist and sometimes including the hand.
arm.ee: She stood with her right arm extended and her palm forward to indicate “Stop!”

around.en: (with the verb "to be") Present in the vicinity.

art.en: The conscious production or arrangement of sounds, colours, forms, movements, or other elements in a manner that affects the senses and emotions, usually specifically the production of the beautiful in a graphic or plastic medium.
art.ee: There is a debate as to whether graffiti is art or vandalism.

ask.en: An act or instance of asking.
ask.ee: I know this is a big ask, but …

attention.ee: Please direct your attention to the following words.

away.en: To depart; to go to another place.
away.ee: At 9 o'clock sharp he awayed to bed.

back.en: The rear of the body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and belly.
back.ee: Could you please scratch my back?

bad.ee: Abducting children is bad for mothers.

ball.en: A solid or hollow sphere, or roughly spherical mass.
ball.ee: a ball of spittle; a fecal ball

base.en: Something from which other things extend; a foundation.
base.ee: The logarithm to base 2 of 8 is 3.

bear.en: A large omnivorous mammal, related to the dog and raccoon, having shaggy hair, a very small tail, and flat feet; a member of family Ursidae.
bear.ee: That window can be a bear to open.

beat.ee: a beat of the heart; the beat of the pulse

become.ee: It hath becomen so that many a man had to sterve.

believe.en: To accept as true, particularly without absolute certainty (i.e., as opposed to knowing)

beside.ee: A small table beside the bed

between.en: A kind of needle, shorter than a sharp, with a small rounded eye, used for making fine stitches on heavy fabrics.
between.ee: I want to buy one that costs somewhere between forty and fifty dollars.

big.en: Someone or something that is large in stature
big.ee: Elephants are big animals, and they eat a lot.

black.en: The colour/color perceived in the absence of light, but also when no light is reflected, but rather absorbed.
black.ee: At this point black makes a disastrous move.

body.ee: a nonpareil face on an agate body

break.en: An instance of breaking something into two or more pieces.
break.ee: The femur has a clean break and so should heal easily.

bring.ee: Waiter, please bring me a single malt whiskey.

build.en: The physique of a human body; constitution or structure of a human body.
build.ee: Rugby players are of sturdy build.

buy.en: Something which is bought; a purchase.
buy.ee: At only $30, the second-hand kitchen table was a great buy.

came.en: Used to indicate that the following event, period, or change in state occurred in the past, after a time of waiting, enduring, or anticipation
came.ee: She’ll be coming ’round the mountain when she comes [...]

care.ee: Care should be taken when holding babies.

carry.en: A manner of transporting or lifting something; the grip or position in which something is carried.
carry.ee: Adjust your carry from time to time so that you don't tire too quickly.

case.en: An actual event, situation, or fact.
case.ee: For a change, in this case, he was telling the truth.

chance.ee: We had the chance to meet the president last week.

change.ee: The product is undergoing a change in order to improve it.

check.en: A situation in which the king is directly threatened by an opposing piece.
check.ee: I don't know if she will be there, but it's worth a check.

choose.en: To pick; to make the choice of; to select.
choose.ee: I chose a nice ripe apple from the fruit bowl.

city.en: A large settlement, bigger than a town; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.
city.ee: São Paulo is the largest city in South America.

class.en: A group, collection, category or set sharing characteristics or attributes.
class.ee: Often used to imply membership of a large class.

clear.en: Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.
clear.ee: a room ten feet square in the clear

close.ee: We owe them our thanks for bringing the project to a successful close.

cold.en: (of a thing) Having a low temperature.
cold.ee: A cold wind whistled through the trees.

color.en: The spectral composition of visible light
color.ee: Humans and birds can perceive color.

come.ee: She’ll be coming ’round the mountain when she comes [...]

common.en: Mutual good, shared by more than one.
common.ee: The two competitors have the common aim of winning the championship.

company.en: A team; a group of people who work together professionally.
company.ee: Keep the house clean; I have company coming.

complete.ee: He completed the assignment on time.

computer.en: A person employed to perform computations; one who computes.

continue.en: An option allowing a gamer to resume play after game over, when all lives have been lost.
continue.ee: Do you want me to continue to unload these?

country.en: (chiefly British) An area of land; a district, region.

course.ee: The normal course of events seems to be just one damned thing after another.

cover.ee: The soldiers took cover behind a ruined building.

cut.ee: He made a fine cut with his sword.

dark.en: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.
dark.ee: The room was too dark for reading.

day.ee: I've been here for two days and a bit.

deal.en: A division, a portion, a share.
deal.ee: We gave three deals of grain in tribute to the king.

decide.en: To resolve (a contest, problem, dispute, etc.); to choose, determine, or settle
decide.ee: Her last-minute goal decided the game.

deep.en: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.

door.en: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. Doors are frequently made of wood or metal. May have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold the door closed and a lock that ensures the door cannot be opened without the key.
door.ee: I knocked on the vice president's door

draw.en: The result of a contest that neither side has won; a tie.
draw.ee: The game ended in a draw.

drive.en: Motivation to do or achieve something; ability coupled with ambition.
drive.ee: Crassus had wealth and wit, but Pompey had drive and Caesar as much again.

drop.en: A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape via surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid.
drop.ee: Put three drops of oil into the mixture.

during.ee: I lived with my parents during the 1970s.

each.en: (operations) An individual item: the least quantitative unit in a grouping.

early.en: A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place early in the day.
early.ee: at eleven, we went for an early lunch;  she began reading at an early age;  his mother suffered an early death

easy.ee: Now that I know it's taken care of, I can rest easy at night.

end.en: The terminal point of something in space or time.
end.ee: At the end of the road, turn left.

enough.ee: Are you man enough to fight me?

even.ee: So let's see. There are two evens here and three odds.

ever.en: Occurring at any time, occurring even but once during a timespan.

example.en: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.

eye.en: An organ through which animals see (perceive surroundings via light).
eye.ee: Bright lights really hurt my eyes.

face.en: The front part of the head of a human or other animal, featuring the eyes, nose and mouth, and the surrounding area.
face.ee: That girl has a pretty face.

fact.en: Something actual as opposed to invented.
fact.ee: In this story, the Gettysburg Address is a fact, but the rest is fiction.

fall.en: The act of moving to a lower position under the effect of gravity.

family.en: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; for example, a set of parents and their children; an immediate family.

far.ee: He went to a far land.

fast.en: A train that calls at only some stations it passes between its origin and destination, typically just the principal stations
fast.ee: That rope is dangerously loose. Make it fast!

feel.en: A quality of an object experienced by touch.

feet.en: A biological structure found in many animals that is used for locomotion and that is frequently a separate organ at the terminal part of the leg.

few.ee: Many are called, but few are chosen.

fight.en: To contend in physical conflict, either singly or in war, battle etc.
fight.ee: A wounded animal will fight like a maniac, relentless, savage and murderous.

figure.en: A drawing or diagram conveying information.
figure.ee: a figure in bronze; a figure cut in marble

fill.en: To occupy fully, to take up all of.
fill.ee: the bucket filled with rain;  the sails fill with wind

find.en: Anything that is found (usually valuable), as objects on an archeological site or a person with talent.
find.ee: I found my car keys. They were under the couch.

fire.en: A (usually self-sustaining) chemical reaction involving the bonding of oxygen with carbon or other fuel, with the production of heat and the presence of flame or smouldering.
fire.ee: We sat about the fire singing songs and telling tales.

first.en: The person or thing in the first position.
first.ee: He was the first to complete the course.

five.ee: He wrote a five followed by four zeroes.

floor.en: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
floor.ee: The room has a wooden floor.

follow.en: (sometimes attributive) In billiards and similar games, a stroke causing a ball to follow another ball after hitting it.

food.en: Any solid substance that can be consumed by living organisms, especially by eating, in order to sustain life.
food.ee: The innkeeper brought them food and drink.

found.en: To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon.
found.ee: I found my car keys. They were under the couch.

four.en: The digit or figure 4; an occurrence thereof.
four.ee: Do you have any more fours? I want to make this a little taller.

free.ee: He was given free rein to do whatever he wanted.

friend.en: A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.
friend.ee: John and I have been friends ever since we were roommates at college.   Trust is important between friends.   I used to find it hard to make friends when I was shy.

front.en: The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves.
front.ee: Officially it's a dry-cleaning shop, but everyone knows it's a front for the mafia.

full.en: Containing the maximum possible amount that can fit in the space available.
full.ee: The jugs were full to the point of overflowing.

game.ee: He's in the securities game somehow.

gave.en: (ditransitive) To move, shift, provide something abstract or concrete to someone or something or somewhere.
gave.ee: I give it a 95% chance of success.

get.ee: I'm going to get a computer tomorrow from the discount store.

give.en: The amount of bending that something undergoes when a force is applied to it; a tendency to yield under pressure; resilence.
give.ee: There is no give in his dogmatic religious beliefs.

gold.en: A heavy yellow elemental metal of great value, with atomic number 79 and symbol Au.
gold.ee: France has won three golds and five silvers.

good.ee: The soup is good and hot.

great.en: A person of major significance, accomplishment or acclaim.
great.ee: Newton and Einstein are two of the greats of the history of science.

ground.en: The surface of the Earth, as opposed to the sky or water or underground.
ground.ee: Look, I found a ten dollar bill on the ground!

group.en: A number of things or persons being in some relation to one another.
group.ee: A group of people gathered in front of the Parliament to demonstrate against the Prime Minister's proposals.

grow.en: To become larger, to increase in magnitude.

hand.en: The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in a human, and the corresponding part in many other animals.

happy.en: A happy event, thing, person, etc.

hard.en: A firm or paved beach or slope convenient for hauling vessels out of the water.
hard.ee: The prisoners were sentenced to three years' hard.

have.ee: I have a house and a car.

head.en: The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth and main sense organs.
head.ee: Be careful when you pet that dog on the head; it may bite.

hear.en: (stative) To perceive sounds through the ear.
hear.ee: I was deaf, and now I can hear.

help.en: Action given to provide assistance; aid.
help.ee: I need some help with my homework.

here.ee: An Alzheimer patient's here may in his mind be anywhere he called home in the time he presently re-lives.

high.en: A high point or position, literally or figuratively; an elevated place; a superior region; a height; the sky; heaven.
high.ee: It was one of the highs of his career.

hold.ee: Keep a firm hold on the handlebars.

hope.en: To want something to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might.
hope.ee: I am still hoping that all will turn out well.

hot.en: (with up) To heat; to make or become hot.
hot.ee: He forgot that the frying pan was hot and burned his hand.

house.en: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
house.ee: This is my house and my family's ancestral home.

how.en: The means by which something is accomplished.
how.ee: I am not interested in the why, but in the how.

human.en: A human being, whether man, woman or child.
human.ee: Humans share common ancestors with other apes.

if.en: An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.
if.ee: If it rains, I shall get wet.

important.ee: It is very important to give your daughter independence in her life so she learns from experience.

in.en: A position of power or influence, or a way to get it.
in.ee: His parents got him an in with the company.

interest.en: The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed.
interest.ee: Our bank offers borrowers an annual interest of 5%.

into.en: To or towards the inside of.

it.en: One who is neither a he nor a she; a creature; a dehumanized being.
it.ee: In the next game, Adam and Tom will be it…

job.ee: A job half done is hardly done at all.

just.ee: It is a just assessment of the facts.

keep.en: The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
keep.ee: He works as a cobbler's apprentice for his keep.

kind.en: A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.
kind.ee: This is a strange kind of tobacco.

know.ee: He knew something terrible was going to happen.

land.en: The part of Earth which is not covered by oceans or other bodies of water.

large.en: An old musical note, equal to two longas, four breves, or eight semibreves.
large.ee: Getting a car tricked out like that will cost you 50 large.

last.en: Final, ultimate, coming after all others of its kind.
last.ee: “Eyes Wide Shut” was the last film to be directed by Stanley Kubrick.

late.en: A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place late in the day or at night.
late.ee: It was late in the evening when we finally arrived.

later.en: Near the end of a period of time.
later.ee: It was late in the evening when we finally arrived.

laugh.en: An expression of mirth particular to the human species; the sound heard in laughing; laughter.
laugh.ee: His deep laughs boomed through the room.

left.ee: The political left is holding too much power.

less.ee: I have less to do today than yesterday.

let.en: The allowing of possession of a property etc. in exchange for rent.
let.ee: After he knocked for hours, I decided to let him come in.

life.en: The state of organisms preceding their death, characterized by biological processes such as metabolism and reproduction and distinguishing them from inanimate objects; the state of being alive and living.
life.ee: Having experienced both, the vampire decided that he preferred (un)death to life.  He gave up on life.

light.en: Visible electromagnetic radiation. The human eye can typically detect radiation (light) in the wavelength range of about 400 to 750 nanometers. Nearby shorter and longer wavelength ranges, although not visible, are commonly called ultraviolet and infrared light.
light.ee: As you can see, this spacious dining-room gets a lot of light in the mornings.

like.en: (usually in the plural) Something that a person likes (prefers).
like.ee: Tell me your likes and dislikes.

line.en: A path through two or more points (compare ‘segment’); a continuous mark, including as made by a pen; any path, curved or straight.
line.ee: The arrow descended in a curved line.

list.en: A strip of fabric, especially from the edge of a piece of cloth.

little.ee: Can I try a little of that sauce?

live.en: To be alive; to have life.
live.ee: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

long.ee: Every uptick made the longs cheer.

love.ee: Hello love, how can I help you?

low.en: Something that is low; a low point.
low.ee: Economic growth has hit a new low.

make.ee: What make of car do you drive?

man.ee: The show is especially popular with middle-aged men.

many.en: A multitude; a great aggregate; a mass of people; the generality; the common herd.
many.ee: Democracy must balance the rights of the few against the will of the many.

map.en: A visual representation of an area, whether real or imaginary.
map.ee: I don't want to play this map again!

may.en: To be strong; to have power (over).
may.ee: you may smoke outside;  may I sit there?

mean.ee: Does she really mean what she said to him last night?

meet.en: A sports competition, especially for track and field (a track meet) or swimming (a swim meet).
meet.ee: OK, let's arrange a meet with Tyler and ask him.

might.en: Power, strength, force or influence held by a person or group.
might.ee: He pushed with all his might, but still it would not move.

mind.ee: Despite advancing age, his mind was still as sharp as ever.

miss.ee: I think I’ll give the meeting a miss.

money.en: A legally or socially binding conceptual contract of entitlement to wealth, void of intrinsic value, payable for all debts and taxes, and regulated in supply.
money.ee: Before colonial times cowry shells imported from Mauritius were used as money in Western Africa.

month.en: A period into which a year is divided, historically based on the phases of the moon.

more.en: To a greater degree or extent.
more.ee: I could no more climb that than fly!

most.ee: The most I can offer for the house is $150,000.

move.en: The act of moving; a movement.
move.ee: A slight move of the tiller, and the boat will go off course.

much.ee: He is much fatter than I remember him.

must.en: Something that is mandatory or required.
must.ee: If you'll be out all day, a map is a must.

name.en: Any nounal word or phrase which indicates a particular person, place, class, or thing.
name.ee: I've never liked the name my parents gave me so I changed it at the age of twenty.

near.en: The left side of a horse or of a team of horses pulling a carriage etc.

need.en: A requirement for something; something needed.
need.ee: I've always tried to have few needs beyond food, clothing and shelter.

never.en: At no time; on no occasion; in no circumstance.
never.ee: I finally finished, and I never want to do that again.

new.ee: Out with the old, in with the new.

next.en: The one that follows after this one.
next.ee: Next, please, don't hold up the queue!

night.en: The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
night.ee: How do you sleep at night when you attack your kids like that!?

no.en: A negating expression; an answer that shows disagreement or disapproval
no.ee: The workers voted on whether to strike, and there were thirty "yeses" and two "nos".

none.ee: I felt none the worse for my recent illness.

north.en: One of the four major compass points, specifically 0°, directed toward the North Pole, and conventionally upwards on a map, abbreviated as N.
north.ee: Minnesota is in the north of the USA.

not.en: A unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true.
not.ee: Did you take out the trash? No, I did not.

nothing.en: Something trifling, or of no consequence or importance.

often.ee: I often walk to work when the weather is nice.

old.en: (with the, invariable plural only) People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group.
old.ee: A civilised society should always look after the old in the community.

once.ee: I have only once eaten pizza.

only.ee: He is the only doctor for miles.

open.ee: an open hand; an open flower

other.en: An other, another (person, etc), more often rendered as another.
other.ee: I'm afraid little Robbie does not always play well with others.

out.en: A means of exit, escape, reprieve, etc.
out.ee: They wrote the law to give those organizations an out.

own.en: Belonging to; possessed; proper to. Often marks a possessive determiner as reflexive, referring back to the subject of the clause or sentence.
own.ee: When we move into the new house, the kids will each have their own bedroom.

page.en: One of the many pieces of paper bound together within a book or similar document.

paper.en: A sheet material used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
paper.ee: a paper of pins, tacks, opium, etc.

people.en: Used as plural of person; a body of human beings considered generally or collectively; a group of two or more persons.
people.ee: There were so many people at the restaurant last night.

perhaps.ee: Perhaps John will come over for dinner.

person.en: An individual; usually a human being.
person.ee: Each person is unique, both mentally and physically.

picture.en: A representation of anything (as a person, a landscape, a building) upon canvas, paper, or other surface, by drawing, painting, printing, photography, etc.
picture.ee: There was a picture hanging above the fireplace.

place.en: (physical) An area; somewhere within an area.
place.ee: I'm in a strange place at the moment.

play.en: Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.

print.en: Books and other material created by printing presses, considered collectively or as a medium.
print.ee: TV and the internet haven't killed print.

public.en: The people in general, regardless of membership of any particular group.
public.ee: Members of the public may not proceed beyond this point.

put.en: A right to sell something at a predetermined price.
put.ee: He bought a January '08 put for Procter and Gamble at 80 to hedge his bet.

quite.en: (heading) To the greatest extent or degree; completely, entirely.

ready.ee: The porridge is ready to serve.

river.en: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
river.ee: Occasionally rivers overflow their banks and cause floods.

run.ee: I just got back from my morning run.

said.ee: The said party has denied the charges.

same.en: Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; identical.
same.ee: Are you the same person who phoned me yesterday?

school.en: (collective) A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
school.ee: The divers encountered a huge school of mackerel.

second.en: Something that is number two in a series.
second.ee: They were discounted because they contained blemishes, nicks or were otherwise factory seconds.

seem.en: To appear; to look outwardly; to be perceived as.
seem.ee: He seems to be ill.   Her eyes seem blue.   It seems like it is going to rain later.   How did she seem to you?

self.en: One individual's personality, character, demeanor, or disposition.
self.ee: one's true self; one's better self; one's former self

several.en: An area of land in private ownership (as opposed to common land).

show.en: A play, dance, or other entertainment.

side.en: A bounding straight edge of a two-dimensional shape.

since.en: From a specified time in the past.

sky.en: The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the ground during the day.
sky.ee: That year, a meteor fell from the sky.

slow.en: Someone who is slow; a sluggard.
slow.ee: a slow train;  a slow computer

small.en: Any part of something that is smaller or slimmer than the rest, now usually with anatomical reference to the back.

some.ee: I guess he must have weighed some 90 kilos.

soon.en: Short in length of time from the present.
soon.ee: I need the soonest date you have available.

south.en: One of the four major compass points, specifically 180°, directed toward the South Pole, and conventionally downwards on a map, abbreviated as S.

speak.en: A low class bar, a speakeasy.

stand.ee: The Commander says we will make our stand here.

still.en: A period of calm or silence.

stop.en: A (usually marked) place where buses, trams or trains halt to let passengers get on and off, usually smaller than a station.
stop.ee: They agreed to meet at the bus stop.

story.en: A sequence of real or fictional events; or, an account of such a sequence.
story.ee: The book tells the story of two roommates.

study.en: (usually academic) To review materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an examination.
study.ee: I need to study my biology notes.

sure.en: Physically secure and certain, non-failing, reliable.
sure.ee: This investment is a sure thing.   The bailiff had a sure grip on the prisoner's arm.

take.en: The or an act of taking.
take.ee: What's your take on this issue, Fred?

talk.en: To communicate, usually by means of speech.
talk.ee: Although I don't speak Chinese I managed to talk with the villagers using signs and gestures.

tell.en: A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a poker game or police interrogation), that reveals information that the person exhibiting the behavior is attempting to withhold.
tell.ee: All told, there were over a dozen.  Can you tell time on a clock?  He had untold wealth.

than.ee: A player than whom none is more skillful.

that.en: Something being indicated that is there; one of those.
that.ee: "The ribbon was that thin." "I disagree, I say it was not that thin, it was thicker... or maybe thinner..."

then.en: Used in comparisons, to introduce the basis of comparison.
then.ee: she's taller than I am;  she found his advice more witty than helpful;  we have less work today than we had yesterday;  We had no choice than to return home

there.ee: You rinse and de-string the green beans; I'll take it from there.

think.en: An act of thinking; consideration (of something).
think.ee: I'll have a think about that and let you know.

three.ee: Put all the threes in a separate container.

through.en: A large slab of stone laid in a dry-stone wall from one side to the other; a perpend.
through.ee: Interstate highways form a nationwide system of through roads.

time.en: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.
time.ee: Time stops for nobody.   the ebb and flow of time

today.ee: Today is the day we'll fix this once and for all.

too.ee: There has been a cutback in federal subsidies. Too, rates have been increasing.

top.en: The highest or uppermost part of something.
top.ee: His kite got caught at the top of the tree.

toward.en: Yielding, pliant; docile; ready or apt to learn; not froward.

town.en: A settlement; an area with residential districts, shops and amenities, and its own local government; especially one larger than a village and smaller than a city.
town.ee: This town is really dangerous because these youngsters have Beretta handguns.

tree.en: Fast growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem.
tree.ee: Birds have a nest in a tree in the garden.

turn.en: (heading) to make a non-linear physical movement.
turn.ee: They say they can turn the parts in two days.

under.ee: Ensure the patient is sufficiently under.

until.en: Up to the time of (something happening).
until.ee: If you can wait until after my meeting with her, we'll talk then.

upon.en: Being the target of an action.
upon.ee: He was set upon by the agitated dogs

use.ee: The use of torture has been condemned by the United Nations.

used.ee: soldiers who are used to hardships and danger

voice.en: Sound uttered by the mouth, especially by human beings in speech or song; sound thus uttered considered as possessing some special quality or character
voice.ee: His low voice allowed him to become a bass in the choir.

walk.en: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times. Compare run.
walk.ee: To walk briskly for an hour every day is to keep fit.

want.ee: What do you want to eat?  I want you to leave.  I never wanted to go back to live with my mother.

water.en: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.
water.ee: By the action of electricity, the water was resolved into its two parts, oxygen and hydrogen.

way.en: (heading) To do with a place or places.
way.ee: You're going about it the wrong way.  He's known for his quirky ways.  I don't like the way she looks at me.

well.ee: I had been sick, but now I'm well.

went.ee: The engine just won't go anymore.

what.en: (Singlish) Used to contradict an underlying assumption held by the interlocutor.

when.en: The time at which something happens.
when.ee: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

where.en: The place in which something happens.
where.ee: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

which.en: (interrogative) What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).
which.ee: By now, you must surely know which is which.

while.en: An uncertain duration of time, a period of time.
while.ee: He lectured for quite a long while.

white.en: The color/colour of snow or milk; the colour of light containing equal amounts of all visible wavelengths.
white.ee: Write in black ink on white paper.

who.en: A person under discussion; a question of which person.
who.ee: I don't know who it is. (indirect question)

why.ee: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

will.en: (now uncommon or literary) To wish, desire (something).

with.en: Along, together with others, in a group, etc.
with.ee: Do you want to come with?

without.en: Outside, externally. This is still used in the names of some civil parishes in England, e.g. St Cuthbert Without.
without.ee: Being from a large, poor family, he learned to live without.

word.en: The smallest unit of language that has a particular meaning and can be expressed by itself; the smallest discrete, meaningful unit of language. (contrast morpheme.)

work.ee: We don't have much time. Let's get to work piling up those sandbags.

world.en: (with "the") Human collective existence; existence in general.
world.ee: There will always be lovers, till the world’s end.

would.en: Something that would happen, or would be the case, under different circumstances; a potentiality.

write.en: The act or style of writing.
write.ee: How many writes per second can this hard disk handle?

year.en: A solar year, the time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
year.ee: we moved to this town a year ago;  I quit smoking exactly one year ago

you.en: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).
you.ee: Both of you should get ready now.

young.en: People who are young; young people, collectively; youth.
young.ee: The young of today are well-educated.

absence.en: A state of being away or withdrawn from a place or from companionship; the period of being away.
absence.ee: Absence makes the heart grow fonder.

accomplish.ee: to accomplish a design, an object, a promise

actual.ee: The actual government expenses dramatically exceed the budget.

aid.ee: He came to my aid when I was foundering.

alleviate.en: To make less severe, as a pain or difficulty.
alleviate.ee: Alcohol is often a cheap tool to alleviate the stress of a hard day.

annual.en: An annual publication; a book, periodical, journal, report, comic book, yearbook, etc., which is published serially once a year, which may or may not be in addition to regular weekly or monthly publication.
annual.ee: I read the magazine, but I usually don't purchase the annuals.

antique.en: A grotesque representation of a figure; a gargoyle.

apply.en: To lay or place; to put (one thing to another)
apply.ee: to apply cream to a rash

appreciate.en: To be grateful or thankful for.

approve.en: To sanction officially; to ratify; to confirm; to set as satisfactory.
approve.ee: Although we may disagree with it, we must nevertheless approve the sentence handed down by the court-martial.

arrange.en: To set up; to organize; to put into an orderly sequence or arrangement.
arrange.ee: to arrange to meet;   to arrange for supper

artificial.ee: The flowers were artificial, and he thought them rather tacky.

aspect.en: Any specific feature, part, or element of something.
aspect.ee: Japan's aging population is an important aspect of its economy.

attach.en: To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively).
attach.ee: An officer is attached to a certain regiment, company, or ship.

automatic.ee: I never learned to drive a stick. I can only drive an automatic.

avoid.en: To try not to meet or communicate with (a person); to shun
avoid.ee: I try to avoid the company of gamblers.

basic.en: A necessary commodity, a staple requirement.
basic.ee: Rice is a basic for many Asian villagers.

blind.en: A covering for a window to keep out light. The covering may be made of cloth or of narrow slats that can block light or allow it to pass.

bore.en: A hole drilled or milled through something, or (by extension) its diameter.

capable.en: Able and efficient; having the ability needed for a specific task; having the disposition to do something; permitting or being susceptible to something.
capable.ee: As everyone knew, he was capable of violence when roused.

cash.en: Money in the form of notes/bills and coins, as opposed to cheques/checks or electronic transactions.
cash.ee: After you bounced those checks last time, they want to be paid in cash.

century.en: A period of 100 consecutive years; often specifically a numbered period with conventional start and end dates, e.g., the twentieth century, which stretches from (strictly) 1901 through 2000, or (informally) 1900 through 1999. The first century AD was from 1 to 100.
century.ee: That was his tenth professional century.

certificate.en: A document containing a certified statement.

chain.en: A series of interconnected rings or links usually made of metal.
chain.ee: He wore a gold chain around the neck.

character.en: A being involved in the action of a story.

chart.ee: Let's chart how we're going to get from here to there.

chemical.en: Any specific chemical element or chemical compound or alloy.

code.en: A short symbol, often with little relation to the item it represents.
code.ee: This flavour of soup has been assigned the code WRT-9.

colleague.en: A fellow member of a profession, staff, academic faculty or other organization; an associate.
colleague.ee: Young Fortinbras,/ Holding a weak supposal of our worth/...Colleagued with the dream of his advantage,/...hath not failed to pester us with message/ Importing the surrender of those lands/Lost by his father. - Hamlet (Act I, Scene 2)

collection.en: A set of items or amount of material procured or gathered together.
collection.ee: The asteroid belt consists of a collection of dust, rubble, and minor planets.

combine.ee: We can't finish harvesting because our combine is stuck in the mud.

comment.ee: I have no comment on that.

conclusion.en: The end, finish, close or last part of something.
conclusion.ee: The board has come to the conclusion that the proposed takeover would not be in the interest of our shareholders.

confident.en: A person in whom one can confide or share one's secrets: a friend.
confident.ee: I'm pretty confident that she's not lying, she's acting normally.

constant.en: That which is permanent or invariable.

consumer.en: One who, or that which, consumes.
consumer.ee: This new system favours the consumer over the producer.

copy.en: The result of copying; an identical duplicate of an original.
copy.ee: Please bring me the copies of those reports.

cost.en: To incur a charge of; to require payment of a (specified) price.
cost.ee: It will cost you a lot of money to take a trip around the world.

crisis.en: A crucial or decisive point or situation; a turning point.

cross.en: A geometrical figure consisting of two straight lines or bars intersecting each other such that at least one of them is bisected by the other.
cross.ee: Put a cross for a wrong answer and a tick for a right one.

current.en: The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.
current.ee: current events;  current leaders;  current negotiations

curve.en: A gentle bend, such as in a road.

customer.en: A patron, a client; one who purchases or receives a product or service from a business or merchant, or intends to do so.
customer.ee: Every person who passes by is a potential customer.

cycle.en: An interval of space or time in which one set of events or phenomena is completed.
cycle.ee: the cycle of the seasons, or of the year

damage.en: Injury or harm; the condition or measure of something not being intact.
damage.ee: The storm did a lot of damage to the area.

decision.ee: It is the decision of the court that movies are protected as free speech.

decrease.en: An amount by which a quantity is decreased.
decrease.ee: One research team has recorded Baishui’s decrease at about 27 meters per year over the last 10 years.

defend.en: To ward off attacks against; to fight to protect; to guard.

delay.en: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.

deliver.en: To set free from restraint or danger.
deliver.ee: deliver a captive from the prison

deny.ee: I wanted to go to the party, but I was denied.

depth.en: The vertical distance below a surface; the degree to which something is deep
depth.ee: Measure the depth of the water in this part of the bay.

description.en: A sketch or account of anything in words; a portraiture or representation in language; an enumeration of the essential qualities of a thing or species.
description.ee: The zoo had no lions, tigers, or cats of any description.

detail.en: Something small enough to escape casual notice.
detail.ee: Note this fine detail in the lower left corner.

disaster.ee: People would suffer disasters when society's morality degenerates.

discover.en: To find or learn something for the first time.
discover.ee: Turning the corner, I discovered a lovely little shop. I discovered that they sold widgets.

display.ee: The trapeze artist put on an amazing acrobatic display.

document.en: An original or official paper used as the basis, proof, or support of anything else, including any writing, book, or other instrument conveying information pertinent to such proof or support.
document.ee: He documented each step of the process as he did it, which was good when the investigation occurred.

domestic.en: A house servant; a maid; a household worker.

doubt.en: Disbelief or uncertainty (about something); a particular instance of such disbelief or uncertainty.

draft.en: A current of air, usually coming into a room or vehicle.
draft.ee: She took a deep draft from the bottle of water.

earn.en: To gain (success, reward, recognition) through applied effort or work.
earn.ee: You can have the s'mores: you earned them, clearing the walkway of snow so well.

electric.en: (usually with definite article) Electricity; the electricity supply.
electric.ee: We had to sit in the dark because the electric was cut off.

emergency.en: A situation which poses an immediate risk and which requires urgent attention.
emergency.ee: Cardiac arrest is an emergency and if you find someone in cardiac arrest you should call 999 immediately.

employ.en: The state of being an employee; employment.
employ.ee: The school district has six thousand teachers in its employ.

encourage.en: To mentally support; to motivate, give courage, hope or spirit.
encourage.ee: I encouraged him during his race.

engine.en: A large construction used in warfare, such as a battering ram, catapult etc.

enormous.en: Deviating from the norm; unusual, extraordinary.

equal.en: A person or thing of equal status to others.

essay.en: (authorship) A written composition of moderate length, exploring a particular issue or subject.

estimate.en: A rough calculation or assessment of the value, size, or cost of something.

event.ee: I went to an event in San Francisco last week.

exceed.ee: The company's 2005 revenue exceeds that of 2004.

exhaust.en: A system consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged; see also exhaust system.
exhaust.ee: Moisture of the earth is exhausted by evaporation.

expect.en: To predict or believe that something will happen

expensive.en: Given to expending a lot of money; profligate, lavish.
expensive.ee: an unnecessarily expensive choice of algorithm

expert.en: A person with extensive knowledge or ability in a given subject.

extreme.en: The greatest or utmost point, degree or condition.

fail.ee: The project was full of fail.

familiar.en: An attendant spirit, often in animal or demon form.

frequent.ee: I am a frequent visitor to that city.

gain.ee: Looks like you've gained a new friend.

gap.en: An opening in anything made by breaking or parting.

general.en: A general fact or proposition; a generality.

genuine.en: Belonging to, or proceeding from the original stock; native

goal.en: A result that one is attempting to achieve.

harsh.ee: Quit harshing me already, I said that I was sorry!

history.ee: History repeats itself if we don’t learn from its mistakes.

honest.en: To adorn or grace; to honour; to make becoming, appropriate, or honourable.

ideal.en: A perfect standard of beauty, intellect etc., or a standard of excellence to aim at.

improve.en: To make (something) better; to increase the value or productivity (of something).
improve.ee: Buying more servers would improve performance.

industry.en: The tendency to work persistently. Diligence.
industry.ee: Over the years, their industry and business sense made them wealthy.

inform.en: To instruct, train (usually in matters of knowledge).
inform.ee: His sense of religion informs everything he writes.

injure.en: To wound or cause physical harm to a living creature.

insist.en: (with on or upon or (that + ordinary verb form)) To hold up a claim emphatically.
insist.ee: I insist that my secretary dresses nicely.

intent.en: A purpose; something that is intended.

introduce.en: (of people) To cause (someone) to be acquainted (with someone else).

invest.en: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.

lack.en: A defect or failing; moral or spiritual degeneracy.

legal.en: The legal department of a company.

link.en: Some text or a graphic in an electronic document that can be activated to display another document or trigger an action.

market.en: A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise at a set time, often periodic.
