massive.en: A homogeneous mass of rock, not layered and without an obvious crystal structure.

material.en: Matter which may be shaped or manipulated, particularly in making something.

mature.en: Fully developed; grown up in terms of physical appearance, behaviour or thinking; ripe.
mature.ee: She is quite mature for her age.

mechanical.en: Manually created layout of artwork that is camera ready for photographic reproduction.

minimum.ee: We need a minimum of three staff members on duty at all time.

mistake.ee: Don't mistake my kindness for weakness.

motion.en: A state of progression from one place to another.

adversary.ee: He prepared to fight his adversary.

antagonism.en: A strong natural dislike or hatred; antipathy.
antagonism.ee: Their longstanding antagonism is manifested in frequent scuffles and shouting matches.

apprentice.en: A trainee, especially in a skilled trade.
apprentice.ee: He was apprenticed to a local employer.

artifact.en: An object made or shaped by human hand or labor.
artifact.ee: The spot on his lung turned out to be an artifact of the X-ray process.

ascendancy.en: The process or period of one's ascent
ascendancy.ee: This was a key moment in Caesar's ascendancy.

bravado.en: A swaggering show of defiance or courage.
bravado.ee: The angry customer stood in the middle of the showroom and voiced his complaints with loud bravado.

breakthrough.en: An advance through and past enemy lines.
breakthrough.ee: Albert Einstein is credited with making some of the greatest breakthroughs in modern physics.

chronicle.en: A written account of events and when they happened, ordered by time.

chasm.en: A deep, steep-sided rift, gap or fissure; a gorge or abyss.

coherence.en: The quality of cohering, or being coherent; internal consistency.

collusion.en: A secret agreement for an illegal purpose; conspiracy.

compromise.en: The settlement of differences by arbitration or by consent reached by mutual concessions.
compromise.ee: a compromise of character or right

conundrum.en: A difficult question or riddle, especially one using a play on words in the answer.

culpability.en: The degree of one's blameworthiness in the commission of a crime or offence.

debacle.en: An event or enterprise that ends suddenly and disastrously, often with humiliating consequences.

delusion.en: A false belief that is resistant to confrontation with actual facts.
delusion.ee: It is far better to grasp the universe as it really is than to persist in delusion, however satisfying and reassuring.

deterioration.en: The process of making or growing worse, or the state of having grown worse.

downfall.en: A precipitous decline in fortune; death or rapid deterioration, as in status or wealth.
downfall.ee: Many economic and political reasons led to the downfall of the Roman Empire.

errand.en: A journey undertaken to accomplish some task.
errand.ee: All the servants were on holiday or erranded out of the house.

estrangement.en: The act of estranging; the act of alienating; alienation.

etiquette.en: The forms required by a good upbringing, or prescribed by authority, to be observed in social or official life; observance of the proprieties of rank and occasion; conventional decorum; ceremonial code of polite society.

exacerbation.en: An increase in the severity of something (such as a disease)

excess.en: The state of surpassing or going beyond limits; the being of a measure beyond sufficiency, necessity, or duty; that which exceeds what is usual or proper
excess.ee: The excess of heavy water was given away to the neighbouring country.

exclusion.en: The act of excluding or shutting out; removal from consideration or taking part.

fervor.en: An intense, heated emotion; passion, ardor.
fervor.ee: The coach trains his water polo team with fervor.

fluency.en: The quality of smoothness of flow.

fragmentation.en: The act of fragmenting or something fragmented; disintegration.

graft.en: A small shoot or scion of a tree inserted in another tree, the stock of which is to support and nourish it. The two unite and become one tree, but the graft determines the kind of fruit.

grievance.ee: If you want the problem fixed, you'll have to file a grievance with the city.

groundwork.en: The foundation; the basic or fundamental parts that support or allow for the rest.
groundwork.ee: The discovery of the laws of electricity laid the groundwork for a century of innovation.

haul.en: An act of hauling or pulling, particularly with force; a (violent) pull or tug.
haul.ee: Getting to his place was a real haul.

hypocrisy.en: The contrivance of a false appearance of virtue or goodness, while concealing real character or inclinations, especially with respect to religious and moral beliefs; hence in general sense, dissimulation, pretence, sham.

impasse.en: A road with no exit; a cul-de-sac

impediment.en: A hindrance; that which impedes or obstructs progress.
impediment.ee: Working in a noisy factory left me with a slight hearing impediment.

indifference.ee: His daughter's indifference towards the sexist group made him wonder if she was even human.

injustice.ee: Silence in the face of gross injustice, or support for it, or even active involvement therein, comes at a price.

irony.en: A statement that, when taken in context, may actually mean something different from, or the opposite of, what is written literally; the use of words expressing something other than their literal intention, often in a humorous context.

kinship.en: Relation or connection by blood, marriage or adoption

longevity.en: The quality of being long-lasting, especially of life.
longevity.ee: Grandfather had incredible longevity: he lived to be 105 years old!

melancholy.en: Black bile, formerly thought to be one of the four "cardinal humours" of animal bodies.

misconception.en: A mistaken belief, a wrong idea
misconception.ee: He had the misconception that the word "misconception" meant becoming pregnant with a girl.

nostalgia.en: A longing for home or familiar surroundings; homesickness.

nuance.ee: Understanding the basics is easy, but appreciating the nuances takes years.

obstruction.en: The act of obstructing, or state of being obstructed.

oppression.en: The exercise of authority or power in a burdensome, cruel, or unjust manner.
oppression.ee: The oppression of the poor by the aristocracy was one cause of the French Revolution.

outrage.en: An excessively violent or vicious attack; an atrocity.

oversight.en: An omission; something that is left out, missed or forgotten.
oversight.ee: A small oversight at this stage can lead to big problems later.

persuasion.en: The act of persuading, or trying to do so; the addressing of arguments to someone with the intention of changing their mind or convincing them of a certain point of view, course of action etc.
persuasion.ee: It is his persuasion that abortion should never be condoned.

pessimism.en: A general belief that bad things will happen.

plethora.en: (usually followed by of) An excessive amount or number; an abundance.
plethora.ee: The menu offers a plethora of cuisines from around the world.

predicament.en: A definite class, state or condition.

prestige.en: The quality of how good the reputation of something or someone is, how favourably something or someone is regarded.
prestige.ee: Oxford has a university of very high prestige.

prudence.en: The quality or state of being prudent; wisdom in the way of caution and provision; discretion; carefulness; hence, also, economy; frugality.

rationality.en: The quality or state of being rational; due exercise of reason; reasonableness.
rationality.ee: His sudden loss of rationality was brought on by excess drink.

reconciliation.en: The reestablishment of friendly relations; conciliation or rapprochement.
reconciliation.ee: He longed for reconciliation with his estranged father, but too many painful memories kept him from making contact again.

reminiscence.en: An act of remembering long-past experiences, often fondly.

resentment.en: A feeling of anger or displeasure stemming from belief that one has been wronged by others or betrayed; indignation.

revelation.en: The act of revealing or disclosing.

scandal.en: An incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the persons or organization involved.
scandal.ee: Their affair was reported as a scandal by most tabloids.

scarcity.en: The condition of something being scarce or deficient

subversion.en: The act of subverting or the condition of being subverted.

unanimity.en: The condition of agreement by all parties, the state of being unanimous.

urgency.en: The quality or condition of being urgent

virtue.en: Accordance with moral principles; conformity of behaviour or thought with the strictures of morality; good moral conduct.
virtue.ee: Without virtue, there is no freedom.

wisdom.en: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.

wrath.ee: Homer relates an episode in the Trojan War that reveals the tragic consequences of the wrath of Achilles.

zeal.en: The fervour or tireless devotion for a person, cause, or ideal and determination in its furtherance; diligent enthusiasm; powerful interest.
zeal.ee: She extols the virtues of veganism with missionary zeal.

abdicate.en: To disclaim and expel from the family, as a father his child; to disown; to disinherit.
abdicate.ee: Note: The word abdicate was held to mean, in the case of James II, to abandon without a formal surrender.

abide.en: To endure without yielding; to withstand; await defiantly; to encounter; to persevere.
abide.ee: The old oak tree abides the wind endlessly.

adhere.en: To stick fast or cleave, as a glutinous substance does; to become joined or united.

adjudicate.en: To settle a legal case or other dispute.

advocate.en: Someone whose job is to speak for someone's case in a court of law; a counsel.
advocate.ee: Since she started working with her advocate, she has become much more confident.

aggravate.en: To make (an offence) worse or more severe; to increase in offensiveness or heinousness.

agitate.en: To disturb or excite; to perturb or stir up (a person).
agitate.ee: He was greatly agitated by the news.

amplify.en: To render larger, more extended, or more intense.

antagonize.en: To work against; to oppose (especially to incite reaction)
antagonize.ee: The other children constantly antagonized Joe to the point of tears.

assimilate.en: Something that is or has been assimilated.
assimilate.ee: Food is assimilated and converted into organic tissue.

banish.en: (heading) To send someone away and forbid that person from returning.

circumvent.en: To avoid or get around something; to bypass

collaborate.en: To work together with others to achieve a common goal.
collaborate.ee: Let's collaborate on this project, and get it finished faster.

commend.ee: The schoolboy was commended for raising the alarm about the burning building.

conciliate.en: To make calm and content, or regain the goodwill of; to placate.

condemn.en: To strongly criticise or denounce; to excoriate the perpetrators of.

contradict.en: To deny the truth of (a statement or statements).

counteract.en: An action performed in opposition to another action.

cultivate.ee: Most farmers in this region cultivate maize.

curtail.en: A scroll termination, as of a step, etc.

deem.en: An opinion, a judgment, a surmise.

deflect.en: To make (something) deviate from its original path.
deflect.ee: The Prime Minister deflected some increasingly pointed questions by claiming he had an appointment.

deteriorate.en: To make worse; to make inferior in quality or value; to impair.

deviate.en: A person with deviant behaviour; a deviant, degenerate or pervert.
deviate.ee: His exhibition of nude paintings deviated from the norm.

disseminate.en: To sow and scatter principles, ideas, opinions, etc, or concrete things, for growth and propagation, like seeds.
disseminate.ee: The values of the human rights movement have disseminated throughout the world.

dissuade.en: To convince not to try or do.
dissuade.ee: Jane dissuaded Martha from committing suicide.

elucidate.en: To make clear; to clarify; to shed light upon.

entail.ee: This activity will entail careful attention to detail.

envision.en: To conceive or see something within one's mind. To imagine.

escalate.en: To increase (something) in extent or intensity; to intensify or step up.
escalate.ee: The shooting escalated the existing hostility.

exaggerate.en: To overstate, to describe more than is fact.
exaggerate.ee: He said he'd slept with hundreds of girls, but I know he's exaggerating. The real number is about ten.

exert.ee: I exerted myself in today's training.

expedite.ee: He expedited the search by alphabetizing the papers.

expel.ee: He was expelled from school multiple times.

frustrate.en: To disappoint or defeat; to vex by depriving of something expected or desired.
frustrate.ee: It frustrates me to do all this work and then lose it all.

hamper.en: A large basket, usually with a cover, used for the packing and carrying of articles or small animals

harness.en: A restraint or support, especially one consisting of a loop or network of rope or straps.
harness.ee: They harnessed the horse to the post.

heighten.en: To make high; to raise higher; to elevate.
heighten.ee: to heighten a flavor or a tint

ignite.en: To set fire to (something), to light (something)

impede.en: To get in the way of; to hinder.

implicate.ee: The evidence implicates involvement of top management in the scheme.

incite.en: To stir up or excite; to rouse or goad into action.
incite.ee: The judge was told by the accused that his friends had incited him to commit the crime.

infer.en: To introduce (something) as a reasoned conclusion; to conclude by reasoning or deduction, as from premises or evidence.

initiate.en: A new member of an organization.

intimidate.en: To make timid or afraid; to cause to feel fear or nervousness; to deter, especially by threats of violence
intimidate.ee: He's trying to intimidate you. If you ignore him, hopefully he'll stop.

negate.en: To deny the existence, evidence, or truth of; to contradict.
negate.ee: The investigation tending to negate any supernatural influences.

nurture.en: The act of nourishing or nursing; tender care

offset.en: Anything that acts as counterbalance; a compensating equivalent.
offset.ee: Today's victory was an offset to yesterday's defeat.

overthrow.en: A removal, especially of a ruler or government, by force or threat of force.
overthrow.ee: I hate the current government, but not enough to want to overthrow them.

overwhelm.en: The state or condition of being overwhelmed.
overwhelm.ee: The dinghy was overwhelmed by the great wave.

perpetrate.en: To be guilty of, or responsible for a crime etc; to commit.

perpetuate.en: To make perpetual; to preserve from extinction or oblivion.

persevere.en: To persist steadfastly in pursuit of an undertaking, task, journey, or goal, even if hindered by distraction, difficulty, obstacles, or discouragement.

preclude.en: Remove the possibility of; rule out; prevent or exclude; to make impossible.
preclude.ee: It has been raining for days, but that doesn’t preclude the possibility that the skies will clear by this afternoon!

proliferate.en: To increase in number or spread rapidly; to multiply.
proliferate.ee: The flowers proliferated rapidly all spring.

provoke.en: To cause someone to become annoyed or angry.
provoke.ee: Don't provoke the dog; it may try to bite you.

reconcile.en: To restore a friendly relationship; to bring back to harmony.
reconcile.ee: to reconcile people who have quarrelled

rectify.en: To heal (an organ or part of the body).

refrain.en: To hold back, to restrain (someone or something).

repudiate.en: To reject the truth or validity of; to deny.

stifle.en: A hind knee of various mammals, especially horses.

tolerate.ee: I can tolerate working on Saturdays, but not on Sundays.

uphold.en: To hold up; to lift on high; to elevate.

vindicate.en: To clear of an accusation, suspicion or criticism.

violate.en: To break or disregard (a rule or convention).
violate.ee: Accessing unauthorized files violates security protocol.

waive.en: To relinquish (a right etc.); to give up claim to; to forego.
waive.ee: If you waive the right to be silent, anything you say can be used against you in a court of law.

achievement.en: The act of achieving or performing; a successful performance; accomplishment
achievement.ee: Finishing the game does not give you a 100% score until you have unlocked all of the achievements.

activity.en: The state or quality of being active; activeness.
activity.ee: Pit row was abuzz with activity.

agriculture.en: The art or science of cultivating the ground, including the harvesting of crops, and the rearing and management of livestock

attitudes.en: The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
attitudes.ee: The ballet dancer walked with a graceful attitude.

career.en: One's calling in life; a person's occupation; one's profession.

cities.en: A large settlement, bigger than a town; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.
cities.ee: São Paulo is the largest city in South America.

civilization.en: An organized culture encompassing many communities, often on the scale of a nation or a people; a stage or system of social, political or technical development.
civilization.ee: Modern civilization is a product of industrialization and globalization.

communication.en: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.

happiness.en: The emotion of being happy; joy.

housing.en: To keep within a structure or container.
housing.ee: The car is housed in the garage.

sport.en: Any activity that uses physical exertion or skills competitively under a set of rules that is not based on aesthetics.
sport.ee: Joe was banned from getting legal help. He seemed to view lawsuits as a sport.

tourism.en: The act of travelling or sightseeing, particularly away from one's home.
tourism.ee: libel tourism; suicide tourism; sex tourism

trade.en: Buying and selling of goods and services on a market.
trade.ee: I did no trades with them once the rumors started.

transportation.en: The act of transporting, or the state of being transported; conveyance, often of people, goods etc.
transportation.ee: We have to get people out of their cars and encourage them to use alternative forms of transportation.

unemployment.en: The state of having no job; joblessness.

urbanization.en: The process of the formation and growth of cities

volunteering.en: To enlist oneself as a volunteer.
volunteering.ee: to volunteer for doing the dishes

workforce.en: All the workers employed by a specific organization or state, or on a specific project

approximately.en: Imprecise but close to in quantity or amount.

drastically.ee: This recession has been drastically different.

enormously.en: Extremely, greatly: to an enormous degree.
enormously.ee: Gloria is enormously pleased with our progress.

gradually.en: In a gradual manner; making slow progress; slowly.

immensely.en: Greatly; hugely; extremely; vastly; to a great extent.

marginally.en: In a marginal manner, or to a marginal extent; barely sufficiently; slightly.

markedly.en: In a marked manner; distinctly, noticeably, conspicuously.
markedly.ee: Being markedly different as a teenager can get you taunted; as an adult it can make you famous.

massively.en: In a massive manner, in a way that appears large, heavy or imposing.

moderately.ee: During the debate, they disagreed plainly, but moderately.

noticeably.ee: We all saw it: he paled noticeably.

overwhelmingly.en: In an overwhelming manner; very greatly or intensely.

partially.en: To a partial degree or extent, incompletely.

predominantly.en: In a predominant manner. Most commonly or frequently by a large margin.
predominantly.ee: The membership is predominantly elderly, 90% are over age 60.

relatively.en: Proportionally, in relation to some larger scale thing.
relatively.ee: He measured his success relatively, that is, competitively.

significantly.en: In a significant manner or to a significant extent.

slightly.ee: He was slightly built, but tall.

substantially.en: In a strong substantial manner; considerably.

sufficiently.ee: Once we had eaten and drunk sufficiently, we padded off to sleep.

virtually.ee: With our medicare supplemental insurance plan, there are virtually no claim forms to fill out. (Advertisement)

widely.en: In a wide manner; across a wide area.

bulk.ee: I understood the bulk of what you were saying, just one of two points I need to hear again.

dataset.en: A file of related records on a computer-readable medium such as disk, especially one on a mainframe computer; a dataset.

distribution.en: An act of distributing or state of being distributed.
distribution.ee: The distribution of my little rock magazine is about 3,000.

estimation.en: The process of making an estimate.

forecast.en: An estimation of a future condition.
forecast.ee: to forecast a rise in prices

fraction.en: A part of a whole, especially a comparatively small part.

gross.ee: The movie grossed three million on the first weekend.

increment.en: The action of increasing or becoming greater.

index.en: An alphabetical listing of items and their location.
index.ee: The index of a book lists words or expressions and the pages of the book upon which they are to be found.

indicator.en: A pointer or index that indicates something.

magnitude.en: The absolute or relative size, extent or importance of something.

margin.en: The edge of the paper, typically left blank when printing but sometimes used for annotations etc.

median.en: A central vein or nerve, especially the median vein or median nerve running through the forearm and arm.

metric.en: A measure for something; a means of deriving a quantitative measurement or approximation for otherwise qualitative phenomena (especially used in engineering).
metric.ee: How to measure marketing? Use these key metrics for measuring marketing effectiveness.

mode.en: One of several ancient Greek scales.
mode.ee: What was the mode of entry?

percentage.en: The amount, number or rate of something, regarded as part of a total of 100; a part of a whole.
percentage.ee: A high percentage of secondary school leavers take a gap year.

proportion.en: A quantity of something that is part of the whole amount or number.
proportion.ee: the proportion of the parts of a building, or of the body

ratio.en: A number representing a comparison between two named things.
ratio.ee: The schoolchildren ganged up to ratio the school catering over its shamefully undemocratic inclusion of vegetables in meals.

sample.en: A part or snippet of something taken or presented for inspection, or shown as evidence of the quality of the whole; a specimen.

scale.en: A ladder; a series of steps; a means of ascending.
scale.ee: Please rate your experience on a scale from 1 to 10.

score.en: The total number of goals, points, runs, etc. earned by a participant in a game.
score.ee: The player with the highest score is the winner.

sum.en: A quantity obtained by addition or aggregation.

threshold.en: The bottom-most part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.

unit.en: A particular, minute unit of mass, defined differently for different substances, but so that varying substances of the same general type have the property that one international unit of the one has the same effect on the human body as one international unit of the other.
unit.ee: The centimetre is a unit of length.

alpine.en: Any of several plants, native to mountain habitats, often grown in a rock garden

altitude.en: The absolute height of a location, usually measured from sea level.
altitude.ee: As the altitude increases, the temperature gets lower, so remember to bring warm clothes to the mountains.

basin.en: A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall

canal.en: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.

cave.en: A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
cave.ee: We found a cave on the mountainside where we could take shelter.

cliff.en: A vertical (or nearly vertical) rock face.

coast.en: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
coast.ee: The rocky coast of Maine has few beaches.

continent.en: Each of the main continuous land-masses on the earth's surface, now generally regarded as seven in number, including their related islands, continental shelves etc.

crater.en: A hemispherical pit created by the impact of a meteorite or other object.
crater.ee: He cratered into that snow bank about five seconds after his first lesson.

crust.en: A more solid, dense or hard layer on a surface or boundary.
crust.ee: You've got a lot of crust standing there saying that.

delta.en: The fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet Δ, δ.

desert.en: (usually in the plural) That which is deserved or merited; a just punishment or reward

dune.en: A ridge or hill of sand piled up by the wind.

earthquake.en: A shaking of the ground, caused by volcanic activity or movement around geologic faults.

elevation.en: The act of raising from a lower place, condition, or quality to a higher; said of material things, persons, the mind, the voice, etc.
elevation.ee: the elevation of grain; elevation to a throne; elevation to sainthood; elevation of mind, thoughts, or character

estuary.en: Coastal water body where ocean tides and river water merge, resulting in a brackish water zone.

forest.en: A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.

gulf.en: A hollow place in the earth; an abyss; a deep chasm or basin.
gulf.ee: the Gulf of Mexico    the Persian Gulf

harbor.ee: The neighborhood is a well-known harbor for petty thieves.

hill.en: An elevated location smaller than a mountain.
hill.ee: The park is sheltered from the wind by a hill to the east.

humid.en: Containing perceptible moisture (usually describing air or atmosphere); damp; moist; somewhat wet or watery.

hurricane.en: A severe tropical cyclone in the North Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, or in the eastern North Pacific off the west coast of Mexico, with winds of 119 km/h (74 miles per hour) or greater accompanied by rain, lightning, and thunder that sometimes moves into temperate latitudes.

island.en: A contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water.
island.ee: an island of colors on a butterfly's wing

isthmus.en: A narrow strip of land, bordered on both sides by water, and connecting two larger landmasses.

lake.en: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.

latitude.en: The angular distance north or south from a planet's equator, measured along the meridian of that particular point.
latitude.ee: His parents gave him a great deal of latitude.

lava.en: The molten rock ejected by a volcano from its crater or fissured sides.

longitude.en: Angular distance measured west or east of the prime meridian.

marsh.en: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass.

mesa.en: Flat area of land or plateau higher than other land, with one or more clifflike edges.
mesa.ee: A few more miles of hot sand and gravel and red stone brought us around a low mesa to the Little Colorado River.

monsoon.en: Any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season.

mountain.en: An elevation of land of considerable dimensions rising more or less abruptly, forming a conspicuous figure in the landscape, usually having a small extent of surface at its summit.
mountain.ee: We spent the weekend hiking in the mountains.

mouth.en: The opening of a creature through which food is ingested.
mouth.ee: "Open your mouth and say 'aah'," directed the doctor.

ocean.en: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
ocean.ee: The island is surrounded by ocean

peninsula.en: A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.

plain.ee: Throughout high school she worried that she had a rather plain face.

polar.en: The line joining the points of contact of tangents drawn to meet a curve from a point called the pole of the line.

ravine.en: A deep narrow valley or gorge in the earth's surface worn by running water.

ridge.en: The back of any animal; especially the upper or projecting part of the back of a quadruped.
ridge.ee: The plough threw up ridges of earth between the furrows.

savanna.en: A tropical grassland with scattered trees

seabed.en: The floor or bottom of the sea or ocean.

shelf.en: A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk etc., and used to support, store or display objects.

shore.en: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
shore.ee: lake shore;  bay shore;  gulf shore;  island shore;  mainland shore;  river shore;  estuary shore;  pond shore;  sandy shore;  rocky shore

slope.en: An area of ground that tends evenly upward or downward.
slope.ee: I had to climb a small slope to get to the site.

soil.en: A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.

spring.en: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching; to overstrain, or stretch injuriously, but without luxation

strait.en: A narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water.

stream.en: A small river; a large creek; a body of moving water confined by banks.
stream.ee: He poured the milk in a thin stream from the jug to the glass.

swamp.en: A piece of wet, spongy land; low ground saturated with water; soft, wet ground which may have a growth of certain kinds of trees, but is unfit for agricultural or pastoral purposes.
swamp.ee: The boat was swamped in the storm.

terrain.en: A single, distinctive rock formation; an area having a preponderance of a particular rock or group of rocks.
terrain.ee: The race will be run over a variety of terrain, including grass and sand.

tide.en: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
tide.ee: The doctor's no good this tide.

topography.en: A precise description of a place.

tundra.en: A flat and treeless Arctic biome.

valley.en: An elongated depression between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.

vegetation.ee: There were large amounts of vegetation in the forest.

volcano.en: A vent or fissure on the surface of a planet (usually in a mountainous form) with a magma chamber attached to the mantle of a planet or moon, periodically erupting forth lava and volcanic gases onto the surface.

waterfall.en: A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
waterfall.ee: A waterfall of mist came from the open freezer.

wilderness.en: An unsettled and uncultivated tract of land in its natural state; a barren land; a wild or waste.

ancient.en: A person who is very old.
ancient.ee: an ancient city  an ancient forest

antiquity.en: Ancient times; faraway history; former ages
antiquity.ee: Cicero was an eloquent orator of antiquity.

archaeology.en: The study of the past by excavation and analysis of its material remains:

barbarism.ee: These barbarisms can not be allowed to continue; they must be crushed or civilization will collapse.

catastrophe.en: Any large and disastrous event of great significance

centuries.en: A period of 100 consecutive years; often specifically a numbered period with conventional start and end dates, e.g., the twentieth century, which stretches from (strictly) 1901 through 2000, or (informally) 1900 through 1999. The first century AD was from 1 to 100.
centuries.ee: That was his tenth professional century.

classical.en: One that is classical in some way; for example, a classical economist.

conquest.en: Victory gained through combat; the subjugation of an enemy.

dynasty.en: A series of rulers or dynasts from one family.

era.en: A time period of indeterminate length, generally more than one year.

excavation.en: The act of excavating, or of making hollow, by cutting, scooping, or digging out a part of a solid mass.

famine.en: Extreme shortage of food in a region.

founder.en: One who founds or establishes (especially said of a company, project, organisation, state)
founder.ee: the founder of Facebook, Mark Zuckerberg

gladiator.en: (in ancient Rome) A person (professional or slave) who entertained the public by engaging in mortal combat with another, or with a wild animal.

indigenous.en: Born or originating in, native to a land or region, especially before an intrusion.

industrialization.en: A process of social and economic change whereby a human society is transformed from a pre-industrial to an industrial state.

legacy.en: Money or property bequeathed to someone in a will.
legacy.ee: John Muir left as his legacy an enduring spirit of respect for the environment.

manuscript.en: A book, composition or any other document, written by hand (or manually typewritten), not mechanically reproduced.

medieval.en: Someone living in the Middle Ages.

mummy.en: An embalmed human or animal corpse wrapped in linen bandages for burial, especially as practised by the ancient Egyptians and some Native American tribes.

pharaoh.en: The supreme ruler of Ancient Egypt; a formal address for the sovereign seat of power as personified by the 'king' in an institutional role of Horus son of Osiris; often used by metonymy for Ancient Egyptian sovereignty

plague.en: (often used with the, sometimes capitalized: the Plague) The bubonic plague, the pestilent disease caused by the virulent bacterium Yersinia pestis.
plague.ee: Ten Biblical plagues over Egypt, ranging from locusts to the death of the crown prince, finally forced Pharaoh to let Moses's people go.

prehistoric.en: Having lasted from a remote period; having been of long duration; of great age, very old.

preservation.en: The act of preserving; care to preserve; act of keeping from destruction, decay or any ill.

reformation.en: An improvement (or an intended improvement) in the existing form or condition of institutions or practices, etc.; intended to make a striking change for the better in social, political or religious affairs or in the conduct of persons or operation of organizations.

relic.en: That which remains; that which is left after loss or decay; a remaining portion.

ritual.en: Rite; a repeated set of actions
ritual.ee: They carried out the ritual carefully.

ruin.en: (sometimes in the plural) The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
ruin.ee: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

shrine.en: A holy or sacred place dedicated to a specific deity, ancestor, hero, martyr, saint, or similar figure of awe and respect, at which said figure is venerated or worshipped.

slavery.en: An institution or social practice of owning human beings as property, especially for use as forced laborers.

temple.ee: a temple of commerce, a temple of drinking and dining

throne.en: An impressive seat used by a monarch, often on a raised dais in a throne room and reserved for formal occasions.

tribe.en: A socially, ethnically, or politically cohesive group of people.

absenteeism.en: The state of being absent, especially frequently or without good reason; the practice of an absentee.

advancement.en: The act of advancing, ; promotion to a higher place or dignity

appraisal.en: The act or process of developing an opinion of value.

apprenticeship.en: The condition of, or the time served by, an apprentice.

bonus.en: Something extra that is good; an added benefit.

commission.en: A sending or mission (to do or accomplish something).

deadline.en: A time limit in the form of a date on or before which something must be completed.
deadline.ee: I must make this deadline or my boss will kill me!

dismissal.en: The act of sending someone away.

ergonomics.en: The science of the design of equipment, especially so as to reduce operator fatigue, discomfort and injury.

freelance.en: Someone who sells their services to clients without a long-term employment contract.

harassment.en: Persistent attacks and criticism causing worry and distress.

hiring.en: To obtain the services of in return for fixed payment.

interview.en: An official face-to-face meeting of monarchs or other important figures.

layoff.en: (chiefly US) A dismissal of employees from their jobs because of tightened budgetary constraints or work shortage (not due to poor performance or misconduct).

moonlighting.en: To work on the side (at a secondary job), often in the evening or during the night.

overtime.en: Working time outside of one's regular hours.

profession.en: A declaration of belief, faith or one's opinion, whether genuine or pretended.

promotion.en: An advancement in rank or position.

qualifications.en: The act or process of qualifying for a position, achievement etc.

retention.en: The act of retaining or something retained

retraining.en: To train again; especially, to train or study in a new subject or job

teamwork.en: The cooperative effort of a team of people to achieve a common goal.

adoption.ee: A Chinese baby girl was given away for adoption.

cohabitation.en: An emotional and physical intimate relationship which includes a common living place and which exists without legal or religious sanction.

guardian.en: Someone who guards, watches over, or protects.

separation.en: The act of disuniting two or more things, or the condition of being separated.

values.en: The quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable.

well-being.en: A state of health, happiness and/or prosperity.

insulation.en: The act of insulating; detachment from other objects; isolation.

transmission.en: The act of transmitting, e.g. data or electric power.

non-proliferation.en: (of a treaty etc) Ending the acquisition of nuclear weapons by countries that do not already have them.

erroneous.ee: His answer to the sum was erroneous.

opaque.en: An area of darkness; a place or region with no light.

questionable.en: Problematic; open to doubt or challenge.

volatile.en: A chemical or compound that changes into a gas easily.

psychology.en: The study of the human mind.

aetiology.en: The establishment of a cause, origin, or reason for something.

biomarker.en: A substance used as an indicator of a biological state, most commonly disease.

artery.en: An efferent blood vessel from the heart, conveying blood away from the heart regardless of oxygenation status; see pulmonary artery.

cerebral.en: Of, or relating to the brain, cerebrum, or cerebral cortex.

diagnostic.en: Any technique used in medical diagnosis.

etiology.en: The establishment of a cause, origin, or reason for something.

genomics.en: The study of the complete genome of an organism

kidney.en: An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine.

muscular.en: Of, relating to, or connected with muscles.

nerve.en: A bundle of neurons with their connective tissue sheaths, blood vessels and lymphatics.

neuropathology.en: The pathology (diseases or study of diseases) of the nervous system

oncogene.en: Any gene that contributes to the conversion of a normal cell into a cancerous cell when mutated or expressed at high levels.

platelet.en: A small colorless disk-shaped particle found in the blood of mammals, which plays an important role in the formation of blood clots.

proteomics.en: The branch of molecular biology that studies the set of proteins expressed by the genome of an organism.

retina.en: The thin layer of cells at the back of the eyeball where light is converted into neural signals sent to the brain.

skeletal.en: Of, or relating to the skeleton

transfusion.en: The transfer of blood or blood products from one individual to another.

transplantation.en: The resettlement of a group of people.

sexism.en: The belief that people of one sex or gender are inherently superior to others.
sexism.ee: The notion that either gender is superior is sexism.

underclass.en: The poorest class of people in a given society.

ageism.en: The treating of a person or people, especially youth or seniors, differently from others based on assumptions or stereotypes relating to their age.

conscription.en: Involuntary labor, especially military service, demanded by some established authority.

curfew.en: Any regulation requiring people to be off the streets and in their homes by a certain time.

despotism.en: Government by a singular authority, either a single person or tight-knit group, which rules with absolute power, especially in a cruel and oppressive way.

elitism.en: The belief that a society or system should be run by an elite.

ghetto.en: An (often walled) area of a city in which Jews are concentrated by force and law. (Used particularly of areas in medieval Italy and in Nazi-controlled Europe.)

nepotism.en: The favoring of relatives or personal friends because of their relationship rather than because of their abilities.
nepotism.ee: Nepotism can get you very far in the world if you've got the right connections.

oligarchy.en: A government run by only a few, often the wealthy.

recidivism.en: Committing new offenses after a crime committed in the past.

biotechnology.en: The use of living organisms (especially microorganisms) in industrial, agricultural, medical and other technological applications.

broadband.en: A wide band of electromagnetic frequencies

disruption.en: An interruption to the regular flow or sequence of something.
disruption.ee: There was great disruption in the classroom when the teacher left.

robotics.en: The science and technology of robots, their design, manufacture, and application

satellite.en: A moon or other smaller body orbiting a larger one.
satellite.ee: A spent upper stage is a derelict satellite.

workflow.en: The rate at which a flow of work takes place

browser.en: A person or animal who browses.

device.en: Any piece of equipment made for a particular purpose, especially a mechanical or electrical one.
device.ee: There are a number of household devices in a kitchen such as a dishwasher, a garbage disposal, or an electric can opener.

domain.en: A geographic area owned or controlled by a single person or organization.
domain.ee: The king ruled his domain harshly.

hyperconnected.en: (of a topological space) That is not the union of two proper closed sets; such that every open set is dense.

keyboard.en: (etc.) A set of keys used to operate a typewriter, computer etc.
keyboard.ee: Keyboarding is the part of this job I hate the most.

multimedia.en: The combined use of sound, video, and text to present an idea.

password.en: A word used to gain admittance or to gain access to information; watchword.

pixel.en: One of the tiny dots that make up the representation of an image in a computer's memory.

ransomware.en: Malware that holds the data of a computer user for ransom, usually requiring or claiming to require payment to restore access.

screen.en: A physical divider intended to block an area from view, or provide shelter from something dangerous.

server.en: A program that provides services to other programs or devices, either in the same computer or over a computer network.

streaming.en: To flow in a continuous or steady manner, like a liquid.
streaming.ee: A flag streams in the wind.

touchpad.en: A flat surface which is sensitive to touch, used mostly in laptop computers to control an on-screen cursor.

username.en: A person's identification on an individual computer system.

webcam.en: A video camera whose output may be viewed in real time over a computer network, especially over the World Wide Web.

website.en: A collection of interlinked web pages on the World Wide Web that are typically accessible from the same base URL and reside on the same server.

wi-fi.en: Any of several standards for short-range wireless data transmission (IEEE 802.11).
wi-fi.ee: I'll send the file using Wi-Fi.
